nodes.title: FUSE Engine
nodes.description: Pure-Rust FUSE kernel protocol engine implementing ABI v7.28 with cross-platform mount runners (Linux fuse3 and macOS macFUSE/FUSE-T), request/response handling, attribute caching, and mount options.
nodes.body:
# FUSE Kernel Protocol Engine

The OIFS FUSE engine is a **pure-Rust implementation of the FUSE kernel ABI v7.28** (major 7, minor 28) with zero external C dependencies. It provides a complete wire parser, frame dispatcher, stateful open-handle table, and cross-platform kernel mount runners for Linux and macOS. The engine multiplexes any number of open FUSE file handles over the single underlying OIFS image file descriptor owned by the `DiskManager`.

## Key Properties

- **Endianness-portable**: Every wire structure uses explicit little-endian `to_le_bytes` / `from_le_bytes` serialization.
- **Dual ABI support**: Simultaneously supports standard Linux 88-byte `FuseAttr` and macOS/Darwin 104-byte `FuseAttr` (with `crtime`, `crtimensec`, `flags`), plus both Linux 8-byte and macOS 16-byte xattr request headers.
- **Single-FD container**: The `FuseHandleTable` multiplexes thousands of FUSE `fh` values over one `.img` OS file descriptor.
- **Strict read-only enforcement**: When mounted read-only (via `DiskManager::is_read_only()` or `FuseMountOptions::read_only`), **every mutating operation returns `-EROFS` with zero disk writes**.
- **Panic-free frame dispatch**: `OifsFuseState::dispatch_frame_for_platform` validates every header and payload boundary and never panics on truncated or malformed input.
- **UTF-8 NFD→NFC normalization**: Transparently normalizes macOS APFS/Finder filenames from NFD to NFC for Linux-compatible directory indices.
- **macOS Finder metadata storm protection**: Fast-rejects `.DS_Store`, `._*`, `.Spotlight-V100`, `.Trashes`, `.fseventsd`, `.TemporaryItems` with `-ENOENT` to prevent metadata churn.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Kernel ["Kernel FUSE Channel"]
        VFS["VFS Layer"]
        Dev["/dev/fuse (Linux) / /dev/macfuseN (macOS)"]
    end
    subgraph Userspace ["OIFS Userspace"]
        Mount["mount(2) / fusermount3 / mount_macfuse"]
        FD["FUSE FD (SCM_RIGHTS)"]
        Session["OifsFuseState / OifsFuseFs"]
        Disk["DiskManager (single .img FD)"]
    end

    VFS --> Dev
    Dev --> Mount
    Mount --> FD
    FD --> Session
    Session --> Disk
```

## FUSE ABI Constants

The engine targets **FUSE kernel protocol version 7.28** with the following wire sizes:

| Structure | Linux ABI Size | macOS ABI Size |
|-----------|----------------|----------------|
| `FuseInHeader` | 40 B | 40 B |
| `FuseOutHeader` | 16 B | 16 B |
| `FuseAttr` | 88 B | 104 B |
| `FuseEntryOut` | 128 B | 144 B |
| `FuseAttrOut` | 104 B | 120 B |
| `FuseSetAttrIn` | 88 B | 128 B (extended) |
| `FuseInitIn` | 16 B | 16 B |
| `FuseInitOut` | 64 B (ABI v7.28) | 64 B |
| `fuse_setxattr_in` / `fuse_getxattr_in` | 8 B | 16 B (adds `position`) |
| `fuse_dirent` header | 24 B | 24 B |

```rust
pub const FUSE_KERNEL_VERSION: u32 = 7;
pub const FUSE_KERNEL_MINOR_VERSION: u32 = 28;
pub const FUSE_ROOT_ID: u64 = 1;
```

The platform-dependent layout is selected via `FuseAbiPlatform`:

```rust
pub enum FuseAbiPlatform {
    Linux,   // 88-byte FuseAttr, 128-byte FuseEntryOut, 104-byte FuseAttrOut
    MacOs,   // 104-byte FuseAttr, 144-byte FuseEntryOut, 120-byte FuseAttrOut
}
```

## Frame Parser & Dispatcher

### Request/Response Headers

`FuseInHeader` (40 bytes) and `FuseOutHeader` (16 bytes) are parsed with explicit bounds checking:

```rust
let Some(hdr) = FuseInHeader::parse(request) else {
    return FuseOutHeader::error_frame(unique, -libc::EINVAL);
};
let payload = &request[FUSE_IN_HEADER_SIZE..];
```

The dispatcher validates:
- `buf.len() >= 40`
- `header.len as usize == buf.len()`
- Opcode is supported (`FuseOpcode::from_u32`)
- Payload length matches declared sizes for each opcode

### Opcode Dispatch

`dispatch_frame_for_platform` matches on `FuseOpcode` and routes to typed handlers:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Kernel
    participant Dispatcher as OifsFuseState::dispatch_frame
    participant Handler as Typed Handler (lookup, read, write...)
    participant Disk as DiskManager

    Kernel->>Dispatcher: Raw frame (header + payload)
    Dispatcher->>Dispatcher: Parse FuseInHeader (40B)
    Dispatcher->>Dispatcher: Validate len == buf.len()
    Dispatcher->>Dispatcher: FuseOpcode::from_u32(opcode)
    alt Unsupported opcode
        Dispatcher-->>Kernel: error_frame(ENOSYS)
    else Supported
        Dispatcher->>Handler: Call typed method (lookup/read/write...)
        Handler->>Disk: DiskManager operation
        Disk-->>Handler: Result / Error
        Handler-->>Dispatcher: FuseEntryOut / FuseAttrOut / data / error
        Dispatcher->>Dispatcher: Encode for platform (Linux/MacOs)
        Dispatcher-->>Kernel: FuseOutHeader + body
    end
```

Supported opcodes (excerpt):

| Opcode | Value | Handler | Read-only check |
|--------|-------|---------|-----------------|
| `Init` | 26 | `handle_init` | No |
| `Lookup` | 1 | `lookup` | No |
| `Getattr` | 3 | `getattr` | No |
| `Setattr` | 4 | `setattr_size` | **Yes** (`-EROFS`) |
| `Mkdir` | 9 | `mkdir` | **Yes** |
| `Unlink` | 10 | `unlink` | **Yes** |
| `Rmdir` | 11 | `rmdir` | **Yes** |
| `Rename` | 12 | `rename` | **Yes** |
| `Open` | 14 | `open` | Write flags → **Yes** |
| `Create` | 35 | `create` | **Yes** |
| `Read` | 15 | `read` | No |
| `Write` | 16 | `write` | **Yes** |
| `Flush` | 25 | `flush` | Only if dirty |
| `Fsync` | 20 | `fsync` | Only if dirty |
| `Setxattr` | 21 | `setxattr` | **Yes** → `-ENOTSUP` |
| `Getxattr` | 22 | `getxattr` | `-ENOTSUP` |
| `Statfs` | 17 | `statfs` | No |
| `Release` | 18 | `release` | No |
| `Opendir` | 27 | `opendir` | No |
| `Readdir` | 28 | `readdir` | No |
| `Releasedir` | 29 | `releasedir` | No |
| `Access` | 34 | `access` | Write mask → `-EROFS` |
| `Destroy` | 38 | `destroy` | No |
| `Forget` | 2 | (one-way) | No |
| `BatchForget` | 42 | (one-way) | No |

One-way notifications (`FUSE_FORGET`, `FUSE_BATCH_FORGET`) return an empty `Vec` — no reply frame is sent to the kernel.

## FUSE Session & State Management

### OifsFuseState

The protocol state machine is `OifsFuseState`, which holds:

| Field | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `options: FuseMountOptions` | Mount configuration |
| `handles: FuseHandleTable` | Open file/directory handle table |
| `parent_map: RwLock<FxHashMap<u64, u64>>` | Child→parent inode mapping for `..` entries |
| `fast_parents: Box<[AtomicU64; 256]>` | Lock-free parent cache (packed child<<32 \| parent) |
| `dir_snapshots: RwLock<VecDeque<...>>` | Sorted directory entry cache (LRU, 8 entries) |
| `append_lock: Mutex<()>` | Serializes `O_APPEND` writes |
| `initialized: AtomicBool` | `FUSE_INIT` completed |
| `destroyed: AtomicBool` | `FUSE_DESTROY` processed |
| `max_write: AtomicU32` | Negotiated `max_write` payload size |

### Lifecycle

<!-- openwiki: mermaid parse failed and this diagram was converted to a text fence so it does not break rendering. Fix the diagram source and restore the mermaid fence. Parser error: Parse error on line 2: ...eated: OifsFuseState::new() Created Expecting 'SPACE', 'NL', 'HIDE_EMPTY', 'scale', 'COMPOSIT_STATE', 'STRUCT_STOP', 'STATE_DESCR', 'ID', 'FORK', 'JOIN', 'CHOICE', 'CONCURRENT', 'note', 'acc_title', 'acc_descr', 'acc_descr_multiline_value', 'CLICK', 'classDef', 'style', 'class', 'direction_tb', 'direction_bt', 'direction_rl', 'direction_lr', 'EDGE_STATE', got 'DESCR' -->
```text
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Created: OifsFuseState::new()
    Created --> Initializing: FUSE_INIT received
    Initializing --> Active: InitOut negotiated (max_write, max_pages)
    Active --> Active: Request/Response dispatch
    Active --> Destroying: FUSE_DESTROY received
    Destroying --> Destroyed: handles.clear(), flush if !RO
    Destroyed --> [*]
    
    note right of Active
        Single-threaded kernel
        FD or multi-threaded
        UnixStream transport
    end note
```

### OifsFuseFs

High-level VFS façade wrapping `Arc<DiskManager>` + `OifsFuseState`. Provides:
- **Binary dispatcher**: `dispatch_frame(&[u8]) -> Vec<u8>`
- **Typed VFS API**: `lookup`, `getattr`, `read`, `write`, `mkdir`, `unlink`, `rename`, `opendir`, `readdir`, `statfs`, `access`, `setxattr`/`getxattr`/`listxattr`/`removexattr` (all `-ENOTSUP`), `open`/`create`/`release`/`flush`/`fsync`

## Handle Table: FuseHandleTable

Maps kernel `fh: u64` → `FuseFileHandle { inode_id, flags, is_dir }`.

- **Lock-free hot path**: 256 SeqLock slots (`fast_slots`) for zero-contention `get(fh)`.
- **Fallback**: `RwLock<FxHashMap<u64, FuseFileHandle>>` for insert/remove and cold lookups.
- **Invalidation**: `invalidate_inode(inode_id)` on unlink/rmdir/overwrite; `clear()` on `FUSE_DESTROY`.

```rust
pub struct FuseFileHandle {
    pub inode_id: u64,
    pub flags: u32,      // POSIX open flags
    pub is_dir: bool,    // true for FUSE_OPENDIR
}
```

## Protocol Negotiation: FUSE_INIT Handshake

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Kernel
    participant OIFS as OifsFuseState::handle_init

    Kernel->>OIFS: FUSE_INIT { major, minor, max_readahead, flags }
    OIFS->>OIFS: Validate major >= 7
    OIFS->>OIFS: minor = min(kernel_minor, 28)
    OIFS->>OIFS: max_readahead = min(kernel, 1MiB)
    OIFS->>OIFS: negotiated_flags = kernel_flags & supported
    OIFS->>OIFS: negotiate_max_write(requested, flags, platform, page_size, linux_max_pages_limit)
    OIFS-->>Kernel: FUSE_INIT_OUT { major:7, minor, max_readahead, flags, max_write, max_pages, time_gran:1ns }
```

### max_write Negotiation

| Platform | Kernel Flags | Effective Cap |
|----------|--------------|---------------|
| **Linux** < 4.20 (no `FUSE_MAX_PAGES`) | — | 128 KiB (32 pages × 4 KiB) |
| **Linux** 4.20–6.12 (`FUSE_MAX_PAGES`) | `max_pages_limit` (default 256) | `max_pages_limit × page_size` |
| **Linux** 6.13+ | `max_pages_limit` (sysfs, up to 1024) | `max_pages_limit × page_size` (up to 4 MiB) |
| **macOS** | `FUSE_BIG_WRITES` required | Requested (default 1 MiB), emitted as `-o iosize=<bytes>` |

`negotiate_max_write` is called with:
- `requested = options.effective_max_write()` (clamped to 4 KiB–4 MiB, 4 KiB aligned)
- `init_flags` from kernel
- `platform = options.abi_platform`
- `page_size = host_page_size()`
- `linux_max_pages_limit = detect_linux_fuse_max_pages_limit()` (reads `/sys/module/fuse/parameters/max_pages_limit`)

## Mount Options: FuseMountOptions

```rust
pub struct FuseMountOptions {
    pub read_only: bool,                    // Enforce -EROFS on all mutations
    pub compression_mode: CompressionMode,  // Applied to FUSE writes
    pub uid: u32,                           // Owner UID in FuseAttr
    pub gid: u32,                           // Owner GID in FuseAttr
    pub attr_ttl_secs: u64,                 // attr_valid TTL (default 1s)
    pub entry_ttl_secs: u64,                // entry_valid TTL (default 1s)
    pub allow_other: bool,                  // allow_other mount option
    pub abi_platform: FuseAbiPlatform,      // Linux / MacOs wire layout
    pub reject_macos_metadata: bool,        // Fast-reject ._*, .DS_Store, etc. (default true)
    pub normalize_nfc: bool,                // NFD→NFC filename normalization (default true)
    pub volname: Option<String>,            // macOS volume name
    pub max_write: u32,                     // Requested max_write (default 1 MiB)
}
```

### OS-Filtered Mount Option Strings

`build_mount_options_for_os(target_os, effective_read_only)` returns `-o` strings:

| Option | Linux | macOS |
|--------|-------|-------|
| `fsname=oifs` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `default_permissions` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `ro` | ✅ (if read_only) | ✅ (if read_only) |
| `allow_other` | ✅ (if requested) | ✅ (if requested) |
| `subtype=oifs` | ✅ | ❌ |
| `noappledouble` | ❌ | ✅ |
| `noapplexattr` | ❌ | ✅ |
| `local` | ❌ | ✅ |
| `iosize=<max_write>` | ❌ | ✅ |
| `volname=<name>` | ❌ | ✅ |

**Key mount options explained**:

- **`default_permissions`**: Enables kernel permission checking based on `uid`/`gid`/`mode` in `FuseAttr` (instead of FUSE daemon doing it). Required for correct multi-user access.
- **`allow_other`**: Allows non-owner users to access the mount (requires `user_allow_other` in `/etc/fuse.conf` on Linux).
- **`ro`**: Kernel-enforced read-only mount; combined with OIFS internal read-only check for defense in depth.
- **`fsname=oifs`**: Sets the filesystem name visible in `df`/`mount` output.
- **`subtype=oifs`** (Linux only): Sets `fstype=fuse.oifs` in `/proc/mounts`.
- **`noappledouble`/`noapplexattr`** (macOS only): Suppresses `._*` AppleDouble files and Apple extended attributes that macFUSE would otherwise synthesize.
- **`iosize`** (macOS only): Tunes the kernel I/O unit size; set to negotiated `max_write`.
- **`volname`** (macOS only): Volume label shown in Finder sidebar.

## Cross-Platform Mount Runners

### Linux: `/dev/fuse` + `fusermount3`

1. **Unprivileged path** (default): `spawn_fusermount_scm_rights`:
   - Creates `socketpair(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM)`
   - Spawns `fusermount3 -o <opts> -- <mountpoint>` with `_FUSE_COMMFD=child_fd`
   - `fusermount3` opens `/dev/fuse`, passes FD via `SCM_RIGHTS` over socketpair
   - Parent receives FD, enters `serve_fuse_fd_with_platform(fd, Linux)`

2. **Privileged fallback**: `mount_linux_direct_dev_fuse`:
   - Opens `/dev/fuse` directly
   - Calls `mount("oifs", mountpoint, "fuse.oifs", MS_NOSUID|MS_NODEV|MS_RDONLY?, "fd=N,rootmode=40000,user_id=...,group_id=...,default_permissions,allow_other?")`
   - Enters `serve_fuse_fd_with_platform(fd, Linux)`

### macOS: `macFUSE` / `osxfuse` (kext) or `FUSE-T` (kext-free NFSv4)

- **Backend discovery**: `discover_macos_fuse_backend()` checks:
  1. `FUSE-T`: `/Library/Application Support/fuse-t/bin/mount_fuse-t` or `go-nfsv4`
  2. `macFUSE`: `/Library/Filesystems/macfuse.fs/Contents/Resources/mount_macfuse`
  3. `osxfuse`: `/Library/Filesystems/osxfuse.fs/Contents/Resources/mount_osxfuse`

- **macFUSE/osxfuse mount flow**:
  1. `socketpair` + `_FUSE_CALL_BY_LIB=1`, `_FUSE_COMMFD=child_fd`, `_FUSE_COMMVERS=2`, `_FUSE_DAEMON_PATH=<exe>`
  2. Spawns `mount_macfuse -o <opts> <mountpoint>` (no positional device arg)
  3. Child passes `/dev/macfuseN` FD via `SCM_RIGHTS`
  4. Parent enters `serve_fuse_fd_with_platform(fd, MacOs)`

- **FUSE-T**: Uses NFSv4 userspace daemon; cannot be served via `/dev/macfuse` FD. Returns error directing to use `serve_fuse_fd`/`serve_stream`/`dispatch_frame` directly.

### serve_fuse_fd (Packet Device Loop)

```rust
loop {
    n = read(fd, buf, buf_len);
    if EINTR/EAGAIN/ENOENT -> continue
    if ENODEV/ECONNRESET/EOF -> Ok(())
    req = &buf[..n];
    resp = dispatch_frame_for_platform(req, platform);
    if !resp.is_empty() { write(fd, resp); }
    if opcode == FUSE_DESTROY -> Ok(())
}
```

- Buffer size: `effective_max_write() + 4096`, clamped to `[128KiB+4KiB, 16MiB]`
- Atomic `read`/`write` per frame (no framing needed on packet devices)
- Retries on `EINTR`, ignores `ENOENT` (interrupted kernel request)

### serve_stream (Unix Stream)

For `AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM`/`SOCK_SEQPACKET` (e.g., tests, IPC):
1. Read 40-byte `FuseInHeader` (exact)
2. Read remaining `header.len - 40` bytes
3. Dispatch, write full response
4. Exit on `FUSE_DESTROY` or clean EOF

## Attribute Caching & TTLs

The kernel caches inode attributes and directory entries based on TTLs returned in `FUSE_LOOKUP`, `FUSE_GETATTR`, `FUSE_SETATTR` responses.

| Cache Type | Struct Field | Default | Configurable via |
|------------|--------------|---------|------------------|
| **Attribute cache** | `FuseAttrOut.attr_valid` / `attr_valid_nsec` | 1 second | `FuseMountOptions.attr_ttl_secs` |
| **Entry cache** (positive) | `FuseEntryOut.entry_valid` / `entry_valid_nsec` | 1 second | `FuseMountOptions.entry_ttl_secs` |
| **Negative entry cache** | `FuseEntryOut.entry_valid` (on `-ENOENT`) | 1 second | Same as positive (`entry_ttl_secs`) |

**Implementation**:

```rust
fn build_entry_out(&self, dm, inode_id, inode) -> Result<FuseEntryOut, i32> {
    Ok(FuseEntryOut {
        nodeid: inode_to_nodeid(inode_id)?,
        generation: 0,
        entry_valid: self.options.entry_ttl_secs,   // <-- TTL
        attr_valid: self.options.attr_ttl_secs,     // <-- TTL
        entry_valid_nsec: 0,
        attr_valid_nsec: 0,
        attr: FuseAttr::from_inode(...),
    })
}
```

- **No explicit invalidation**: OIFS relies on short TTLs (default 1s) for coherence. For lower latency, reduce TTLs; for less kernel→userspace traffic, increase them.
- **`generation: 0`**: Not used (would require kernel `FUSE_INIT` `FUSE_EXPORT_SUPPORT` + `FUSE_HANDLE_KILLPRIV_V2` which OIFS doesn't advertise).

## macOS-Specific Behaviors

### FUSE-T vs macFUSE/osxfuse

| Aspect | FUSE-T (kext-free) | macFUSE / osxfuse (kext) |
|--------|-------------------|-------------------------|
| **Mechanism** | NFSv4 userspace daemon | Kernel extension + `/dev/macfuseN` |
| **OIFS mount support** | ❌ (cannot serve via FD) | ✅ via `mount_macfuse`/`mount_osxfuse` |
| **Wire ABI** | N/A (NFSv4) | macOS 104-byte `FuseAttr` |
| **Detection** | `discover_macos_fuse_backend()` | Same |

### macOS Finder Metadata Storm Protection

When `reject_macos_metadata = true` (default), these filenames are rejected at VFS entry with `-ENOENT`:

- `._*` (AppleDouble resource forks)
- `.DS_Store`
- `.Spotlight-V100`
- `.Trashes`
- `.fseventsd`
- `.TemporaryItems`

This prevents Finder/Spotlight from creating thousands of metadata files inside the OIFS container.

### UTF-8 NFD → NFC Normalization

When `normalize_nfc = true` (default), incoming filenames are normalized:

- **Input**: NFD (decomposed) as emitted by macOS APFS/Finder (e.g., `e` + `´` = 2 codepoints)
- **Output**: NFC (composed) as expected by Linux/OIFS directory indices (e.g., `é` = 1 codepoint)
- **Fast path**: ASCII and already-composed strings returned as `Cow::Borrowed` (zero allocation)
- **Supported compositions**: Hangul Jamo (L+V→LV, LV+T→LVT), Japanese Kana dakuten/handakuten, Latin/Cyrillic combining diacritics

## Extended Attributes (xattr)

**Unsupported on OIFS**. All xattr operations return `-ENOTSUP` (not `-ENOSYS` or `-EINVAL`, which would cause macOS Finder copies to abort):

| Opcode | Handler | Returns |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `SETXATTR` | `setxattr` | `-ENOTSUP` (or `-EROFS` if read-only) |
| `GETXATTR` | `getxattr` | `-ENOTSUP` |
| `LISTXATTR` | `listxattr` | `-ENOTSUP` |
| `REMOVEXATTR` | `removexattr` | `-ENOTSUP` (or `-EROFS` if read-only) |

Wire headers parsed for both Linux (8B) and macOS (16B with `position` for resource forks).

## Read-Only Enforcement

Two-layer defense:

1. **Mount option** `ro` / `FuseMountOptions.read_only`: Kernel blocks write syscalls at VFS layer.
2. **OIFS internal check**: `is_read_only(dm)` = `dm.is_read_only() || options.read_only`. Every mutating handler (`setattr_size`, `mkdir`, `unlink`, `rmdir`, `rename`, `open` with write flags, `create`, `write`, `setxattr`, `removexattr`, `flush`/`fsync` if dirty) returns `-EROFS` **before any disk access**.

```rust
fn is_read_only(&self, dm: &DiskManager) -> bool {
    dm.is_read_only() || self.options.read_only
}

pub fn write(&self, ...) -> Result<u32, i32> {
    if self.is_read_only(dm) { return Err(-libc::EROFS); }
    ...
}
```

## SCM_RIGHTS File Descriptor Passing

Used by both Linux `fusermount3` and macOS `mount_macfuse` to pass the kernel FUSE device FD to the userspace daemon.

```rust
pub fn send_fd_scm_rights(sock_fd: RawFd, fd: RawFd) -> io::Result<()>
pub fn recv_fd_scm_rights(sock_fd: RawFd) -> io::Result<OwnedFd>
```

- Ancillary data: `cmsg_level=SOL_SOCKET`, `cmsg_type=SCM_RIGHTS`
- `sendmsg`/`recvmsg` with `CMSG_SPACE`/`CMSG_LEN` calculations
- Linux: uses `MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC` on receive
- Sets `FD_CLOEXEC` on received FD

## Formal Verification (Kani)

The engine includes Kani proofs for critical invariants:

| Proof | Property |
|-------|----------|
| `proof_fuse_nodeid_inode_bijection_and_root_mapping` | `inode_to_nodeid` / `nodeid_to_inode` form strict bijection; root `0 ↔ 1`; `u64::MAX` rejected |
| `proof_fuse_dirent_align_and_record_bounds` | `fuse_dirent_align(24 + name_len)` always multiple of 8, `≥ unaligned`, `< unaligned + 8` |
| `proof_fuse_frame_header_parse_no_panic_and_bounds` | `FuseInHeader::parse` never panics; rejects `<40B`; rejects `len != buf.len()` |

## Usage Examples

### Programmatic Frame Dispatch

```rust
let dm = DiskManager::open("data.oifs", 100_000_000)?;
let opts = FuseMountOptions::for_host_kernel();
let fuse_fs = OifsFuseFs::new(dm, opts);

// Raw binary frame dispatch (for custom transports)
let request = build_lookup_frame(1, FUSE_ROOT_ID, "hello.txt");
let response = fuse_fs.dispatch_frame(&request);
```

### Kernel Mount (Linux)

```rust
let dm = DiskManager::open("data.oifs", 100_000_000)?;
let opts = FuseMountOptions {
    read_only: false,
    allow_other: true,
    ..FuseMountOptions::for_host_kernel()
};
let fuse_fs = OifsFuseFs::new(dm, opts);
fuse_fs.mount("/mnt/oifs")?;  // Spawns fusermount3, serves until unmount
```

### Kernel Mount (macOS)

```rust
let dm = DiskManager::open("data.oifs", 100_000_000)?;
let opts = FuseMountOptions {
    volname: Some("MyOIFS".into()),
    ..FuseMountOptions::for_host_kernel()  // abi_platform = MacOs
};
let fuse_fs = OifsFuseFs::new(dm, opts);
fuse_fs.mount("/Volumes/MyOIFS")?;  // Uses mount_macfuse + SCM_RIGHTS
```

### Userspace-Only (No Kernel Mount)

```rust
let dm = DiskManager::open("data.oifs", 100_000_000)?;
let opts = FuseMountOptions::default();
let fuse_fs = OifsFuseFs::new(dm, opts);

// Serve over Unix domain socket pair
let (client, server) = UnixStream::pair()?;
std::thread::spawn(move || fuse_fs.serve_stream(&mut server));
// Client speaks FUSE ABI v7.28 over the socket
```

### Custom max_write

```rust
let opts = FuseMountOptions {
    max_write: 4 * 1024 * 1024,  // Request 4 MiB (clamped by kernel)
    ..FuseMountOptions::default()
};
```

## Related Pages

- [Async I/O & Pluggable Engines](async_io_and_engines.md) — Data block read engines (mmap/pread/io_uring)
- [Concurrency and Session](concurrency_and_session.md) — Multi-process coordination, master election
- [Architecture Overview](../architecture/overview.md) — System-wide component diagram

nodes.title: Architecture
nodes.body:
# Files

- [Async I/O & Pluggable Engines](async_io_and_engines.md) - Covers the pluggable I/O engine abstraction (Mmap, Pread, IoUring), extent coalescing, io_uring capability gating, async read engine with inline fast-path (Mmap, DataPageCache, ChunkReadCache, DecodedBlobCache), OifsAsyncTask, group-commit write pipeline, and ReadSession/FileReadHandle for concurrent reads.
- [Block & Inode Allocation](block_allocation.md) - Documents the bitmap-based block allocator (SimpleBlockAllocator), inode allocator, free space tracking, allocation strategies (hints, contiguous runs), multi-block bitmap layout (v3), hardware-accelerated tzcnt scanning, BitmapSliceMut write-through mirrors for FileIo mode, and allocation simulation for WAL transactions.
- [Compression & Pre-Compression Filters](compression_and_filters.md) - Seekable 64 KiB chunked compression (Zstd), SIMD pre-filters (Delta, Shuffle, BitShuffle, TruncPrecision), ZstdContextPool with persistent scoped worker pool, DecodedBlobCache and ChunkReadCache for read acceleration, and cache invalidation across write/truncate/defrag.
- [Concurrency and session](concurrency_and_session.md)
- [Online Defragmentation and Auto-Defrag](defragmentation.md) - How OIFS analyzes filesystem fragmentation using 64-bit bitmap scanning and performs both safe (out-of-place rebuild with atomic rename) and WAL-atomic in-place defragmentation, including ChunkEntry relocation for seekable files, shift_table_collapse for chunk table compaction, and a background auto-defrag coordinator.
- [DiskManager & Persistence](disk_manager_and_persistence.md) - Central coordinator for OIFS storage: image open/create, superblock management, inode CRUD, data read/write with compression/encryption, durability modes, flush/msync, read-only mounts, and atomic rename.
- [Encryption & Filename Obfuscation](encryption.md) - Argon2id KDF, BLAKE2b-512 subkeys, XChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD for data, 192-bit SIV for filenames, and key management.
- [C FFI & C++ API](ffi_interface.md) - Documents the public C FFI (oifs.h) and modern C++17/20 header-only API (oifs.hpp): opaque handles, error codes, sync/async operations, PinnableSlice zero-copy views, and co_await integration.
- [FUSE Engine](fuse_engine.md) - Pure-Rust FUSE kernel protocol engine implementing ABI v7.28 with cross-platform mount runners (Linux fuse3 and macOS macFUSE/FUSE-T), request/response handling, attribute caching, and mount options.
- [Inode Layout and Multi-Block Directories](inode_and_directory.md) - Detailed specification of OIFS's 256-byte inode structure (format v2), directory entry format with filename encryption, block pointer hierarchy (BlockPath), multi-block directory structure with SipHash-2-4 indexing, and directory cache interactions.
- [Filesystem Integrity Checking (fsck)](integrity_checking_fsck.md) - How the OIFS fsck structural consistency scanner performs set-theoretic verification between bitmap allocation states and directory reachability to detect orphan inodes, leaked blocks, missing blocks, cross-linked blocks, and corrupted inodes, plus read-only journal cleanliness verification. Covers chunk reference validation, deduplication detection, repair strategies, and verification flow.
- [Metadata WAL / Journaling](journal.md)
- [MCP Server (oifs_mcp)](mcp_server.md) - How the oifs_mcp binary exposes the OIFS storage engine as Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools over stdio, providing AI agents with an isolated, single-file virtual filesystem for persistent memory.
- [NFSv3 Server](nfs_server.md) - Pure-Rust local loopback NFSv3 server implementing ONC RPC v2, XDR, MOUNT v3, and NFS v3 procedures for zero-kext mounting on macOS and unprivileged Linux.
- [Architecture Overview](overview.md) - High-level system map showing owned subsystems, runtime domains, and cross-system data flows for OIFS.
- [Rename & Atomic Operations](rename_and_atomic_ops.md) - Documents the atomic POSIX rename implementation with WAL transactions, SIV re-encryption for cross-directory moves on encrypted filesystems, FUSE_RENAME/RENAME2 opcode handling, and the MetadataOp journal framing for create/delete/mkdir/rename.
- [Storage Engines](storage_engines.md) - OIFS dual storage backends—Mmap (zero-copy MAP_SHARED/PROT_READ) and FileIo (pread/pwrite + 64-shard DataPageCache)—operating over the exact same on-disk format. Covers mode selection, trade-offs, cache interactions, and coherence protocols.
- [Superblock & On-Disk Layout](superblock_and_layout.md) - Comprehensive documentation of the OIFS superblock structure, format versioning (v1/v2/v3), block layout geometry, journal region placement, encryption fields, and migration cursor mechanics for in-place format upgrades.

## Responsibility and ownership

The inode and directory subsystem defines the structural foundation of the OIFS filesystem across these modules:

<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../src/inode.rs#L10-L15] file "../src/inode.rs" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
- [`src/inode.rs`](../src/inode.rs): Defines the 256-byte fixed-size [`Inode`](../src/inode.rs#L33-L69) struct, the [`FileType`](../src/inode.rs#L10-L15) discrimination model, block pointer tiers, encryption nonces, filter flags, chunked compression support, and `ChunkEntry` bit layout.

- [`src/inode_format.rs`](../src/inode_format.rs): Implements deterministic on-disk encoding/decoding for the **format v2** 256-byte inode record (`INODE_SLOT_SIZE = 256`), including the frozen field layout `[0..166)`, `record_version` at offset 166, `flags` (u32) at offset 167, CRC32C at offset 171, and zero-filled padding to byte 256. Legacy v1 (`bincode`) decoding is retained for backward compatibility.

Also provides SipHash-2-4 filename hashing for fast filtering.

- [`src/encryption.rs`](../src/encryption.rs): Implements deterministic filename encryption via 192-bit SIV nonce (`derive_filename_siv_nonce`), XChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD with `parent_inode` bound in AAD (`filename_aad_stack`), and Base64URL `_e_` prefix encoding. Legacy v1 (12-byte nonce) fallback is supported.

- [`src/fuse.rs`](../src/fuse.rs): Implements UTF-8 NFD→NFC filename normalization for macOS FUSE compatibility, filtering macOS metadata filenames (`._*`, `.DS_Store`, etc.), and providing the FUSE VFS layer backed by `DiskManager`.

- [`src/superblock.rs`](../src/superblock.rs): Manages filesystem layout, format versioning (`format_version`), and inode table placement. Controls whether inodes use legacy v1 or fixed v2 format via `inode_record_version_for()`.

---

## The 256-byte Inode structure (format v2)

<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../src/inode.rs#L33-L69] file "../src/inode.rs" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
Every file and directory in OIFS is represented by an [`Inode`](../src/inode.rs#L33-L69) stored within the contiguous Inode Table starting at `superblock.inode_table_block`. The on-disk format is **format v2**: a deterministic 256-byte record (`INODE_SLOT_SIZE = 256`) with frozen field offsets `[0..166)`, a `record_version` byte at offset 166, `flags` (u32) at offset 167, CRC32C at offset 171, and zero padding to byte 256. The in-memory `#[repr(C)]` struct mirrors this layout.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct Inode {
    /// Type of this inode (File or Directory)
    pub mode: FileType,
    /// Logical size in bytes (original/uncompressed size)
    pub size: u64,
    /// Physical size in bytes if compressed, 0 if stored raw
    pub compressed_size: u64,
    /// Creation timestamp (Unix epoch seconds)
    pub created_at: u64,
    /// Last modification timestamp (Unix epoch seconds)
    pub modified_at: u64,
    /// Direct block pointers (10 blocks) + single indirect (blocks[10]) + double indirect (blocks[11])
    /// Block ID 0 indicates unallocated/empty block
    pub blocks: [u64; 12],

    // Encryption fields
    /// Is this file encrypted?
    pub encrypted: bool,
    /// Nonce for XChaCha20-Poly1305 (24 bytes, unique per file)
    pub encryption_nonce: [u8; 24],

    // Pre-compression filter fields (blosc2-style pipeline)
    /// Element size for shuffle/delta filters (1, 2, 4, or 8 bytes). 0 = no filters.
    pub filter_typesize: u8,
    /// Whether delta encoding was applied before compression
    pub filter_delta: bool,
    /// Whether byte shuffle was applied before compression
    pub filter_shuffle: bool,
    /// Whether bit shuffle was applied before compression
    pub filter_bitshuffle: bool,

    /// Triple indirect block pointer for files > 1GB (supports up to 513GB)
    pub triple_indirect: u64,

    /// Extended inode flags (e.g. INODE_FLAG_SEEKABLE_64K)
    pub flags: u32,
}
```

### On-disk format v2 record layout (fixed 256 bytes)

```text
[0]           u8     mode tag (0 = File, 1 = Directory)
[1..9]        u64    size                  (logical / uncompressed)
[9..17]       u64    compressed_size       (physical, 0 when stored raw)
[17..25]      u64    created_at
[25..33]      u64    modified_at
[33..129]     12×u64 block pointers (direct[0..9], single[10], double[11])
[129]         u8     encrypted flag (0/1)
[130..154]    24B    encryption_nonce (XChaCha20-Poly1305)
[154]         u8     filter_typesize
[155]         u8     filter_delta
[156]         u8     filter_shuffle
[157]         u8     filter_bitshuffle
[158..166]    u64    triple_indirect
[166]         u8     record_version (2 = legacy v2 no CRC, 3 = v3 with CRC32C)
[167..171]    u32    flags (extended inode flags)
[171..175]    u32    crc32c (CRC32C over bytes [0..171) when record_version == 3)
[175..256]    zero padding (reserved for future additive fields)
```

**Field stability guarantee**: Offsets `[0..166)` are frozen for all revisions ≥ 2. New fields may only be appended into the reserved tail `[167..256)`; existing offsets must never move, or every previously written record becomes unreadable.

### Versioning

Two independent version numbers gate decoding:

- **SuperBlock `format_version`** selects the *decoder family*. `1` means the historical `bincode` layout (no self-describing version byte); `≥ 2` means the fixed 256-byte record described here.
- **`record_version`** (inode_format.rs) selects the record revision *within* the fixed family, making future formats additive.

The split matters because a version byte alone cannot bootstrap the v1 → v2 step: a v1 `bincode` record and a v2 record are not reliably distinguishable by inspection, so the superblock has to say which decoder to use. Once inside the fixed family, `record_version` lets a future v3 append fields at offsets ≥ 166 without moving any existing field, so a v3 image can be migrated lazily one record at a time.

### Encoding / Decoding

- `encode_v2()` produces a fully deterministic 256-byte record with zero-filled padding.
- `decode_v2()` validates the file-type tag, verifies CRC32C when `record_version == 3`, and rejects unknown tags rather than guessing.
- `encode_for()` / `decode_for()` dispatch based on superblock `format_version`, preserving v1 compatibility for unmigrated images.

---

## ChunkEntry: 64KB Seekable Compression

When an inode has `INODE_FLAG_SEEKABLE_64K` set (`0x0001`), each 64-bit slot in `blocks[0..12]` (and indirect blocks) represents a **64KB logical chunk** rather than a single 4KB block. This enables random access within compressed files.

```rust
#[repr(transparent)]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ChunkEntry(pub u64);
```

### Bit layout (64 bits)

| Bits | Field | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| 0..32 | `start_block: u32` | Physical start block on disk |
| 32..40 | `block_count: u8` | Number of contiguous 4KB blocks allocated (1..16) |
| 40..48 | `flags: u8` | Chunk state: `FLAG_EMPTY=0`, `FLAG_COMPRESSED=1`, `FLAG_RAW=2` |
| 48..64 | `compressed_len: u16` | Exact compressed byte length (≤ 65535) |

**State predicates**:
- `is_empty()`: `raw == 0 || flags == FLAG_EMPTY` (sparse hole)
- `is_compressed()`: `flags == FLAG_COMPRESSED` (Zstd compressed)
- `is_raw()`: `flags == FLAG_RAW` (uncompressed fallback when compression inflates)

Each chunk maps up to 16 × 4KB = 64KB physical blocks, matching the logical chunk size. The `compressed_len` allows the reader to know exactly how many bytes to read and decompress.

---

## BlockPath: Hierarchical Block Addressing

<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../src/inode.rs#L203-L228] file "../src/inode.rs" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
OIFS uses a 4-tier block pointer hierarchy (direct, single indirect, double indirect, triple indirect) to address up to ~513GB per file (4KB blocks). The [`BlockPath`](../src/inode.rs#L203-L228) enum decomposes a logical block index into the exact pointer-tree slots.

```rust
pub enum BlockPath {
    Direct(usize),      // inode.blocks[i]              (0 ≤ i < 10)
    Single(usize),      // inode.blocks[10] -> slot i   (0 ≤ i < 512)
    Double(usize, usize), // inode.blocks[11] -> a -> b (0 ≤ a,b < 512)
    Triple(usize, usize, usize), // inode.triple_indirect -> a -> b -> c (0 ≤ a,b,c < 512)
}
```

### Tier boundaries (constants)

```rust
const DIRECT_BLOCKS: usize = 10;         // blocks[0..9]
const PTRS_PER_BLOCK: usize = 512;       // 4096 / 8
const SINGLE_END: usize = DIRECT_BLOCKS + PTRS_PER_BLOCK;                    // 522
const DOUBLE_END: usize = SINGLE_END + PTRS_PER_BLOCK * PTRS_PER_BLOCK;      // 262,666
const MAX_LOGICAL_BLOCKS: usize = DOUBLE_END + PTRS_PER_BLOCK^3;             // ~134M blocks (~513GB)
```

### Decomposition / reconstruction

```rust
BlockPath::from_logical(idx)  // logical block index → BlockPath
BlockPath::to_logical(self)   // BlockPath → logical block index (inverse)
BlockPath::slots_in_bounds(self) // validates all indices < PTRS_PER_BLOCK
```

The decomposition is **provably correct** via Kani symbolic verification: for every possible logical block index, the pointer-tree decomposition never produces an out-of-bounds slot and is exactly invertible (no two logical blocks map to the same physical pointer slot, and none is skipped). The Kani harness exhaustively verifies tier boundaries and round-trip properties.

---

## Directory Entry Format

A directory is stored as a sequence of variable-length `DirectoryEntry` records in one or more 4KB data blocks. The on-disk wire format per entry:

```text
[0..8]     u64  inode_id
[8..16]    u64  hash (SipHash-2-4 of plaintext filename; 0 = legacy/unhashed)
[16..18]   u16  name_len (1..255)
[18..]     bytes  name (UTF-8, no NUL, no '/', no '\', not "." or "..")
```

Entries are packed contiguously; a `name_len == 0` marks the end of valid entries (remaining bytes are zero). The max filename length is 255 bytes (`DirectoryEntry::MAX_FILENAME_LEN`).

### SipHash-2-4 for fast filtering

```rust
pub fn hash_filename(name: &str) -> u64;
pub fn hash_filename_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> u64;
```

The hash is stored in each directory entry. During lookup, `find_entry_in_block_with_hash()` first compares the precomputed target hash against the stored entry hash (if both are non-zero) — a single `u64` comparison — before doing the string `memcmp`. This turns most negative lookups into a single 8-byte integer compare per entry, avoiding UTF-8 string comparisons.

**SipHash-2-4 parameters** (fixed, deterministic):
- `k0 = 0x0706050403020100`, `k1 = 0x0f0e0d0c0b0a0908`
- Initialization constants: `0x736f6d6570736575`, `0x646f72616e646f6d`, `0x6c7967656e657261`, `0x7465646279746573`

The hash is **not cryptographic**; it is a fast, deterministic filter. Collisions merely fall back to string comparison.

### Zero-allocation lookup primitives

All directory scans operate on raw `&[u8]` slices with zero heap allocation:

- `find_entry_in_block(slice, name)` — linear scan, string compare only
- `find_entry_in_block_with_hash(slice, name, hash)` — hash filter + string compare
- `find_insert_offset_in_block(slice)` — finds append position (end of last entry)
- `remove_entry_in_block_bytes(slice, name, hash)` — in-place removal, compacts entries forward, zeroes tail
- `has_valid_entry_in_block(slice)` — returns true if ≥ 1 valid entry
- `for_each_valid_inode_in_block(slice, f)` — visitor for `fsck` (yields inode IDs)

---

## Multi-Block Directories and SipHash Indexing

A directory can span up to `MAX_DIR_BLOCKS = 65,536` blocks (256 MB directory table, supporting millions of files). The directory inode's `blocks[]` array and `size` field encode the block list:

```rust
pub fn dir_block_count(size: u64, first_block: u64, block_size: u64) -> usize {
    if block_size == 0 { return 0; }
    if size == 0 {
        usize::from(first_block != 0)  // legacy: 1 block
    } else {
        (size.div_ceil(block_size) as usize).min(MAX_DIR_BLOCKS)
    }
}
```

**Legacy v1 single-block directories** used `blocks[0]` only and stored `size == 0`. The `size == 0 && first_block != 0` pattern implies exactly one block.

### DirIndex: In-memory directory cache

<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../src/disk/caches.rs#L301-L328] file "../src/disk/caches.rs" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
To avoid repeated full-directory scans, each directory gets a [`DirIndex`](../src/disk/caches.rs#L301-L328) when promoted:

```rust
pub(crate) struct DirIndex {
    pub(crate) complete: bool,              // true once every on-disk entry is in `plain`
    pub(crate) plain_complete: bool,
    pub(crate) cold_scans: u32,             // counts full scans before promotion
    pub(crate) may_have_holes: bool,        // earlier blocks may have free space from deletions
    pub(crate) tail_offset: Option<(u64, u16)>, // (physical_block_id, next_insert_offset) for O(1) append
    pub(crate) stored: FxHashMap<String, (u64, u64, u64)>, // ciphertext name → (inode, block_id, stored_hash)
    pub(crate) plain: FxHashMap<String, (u64, u64)>,       // plaintext name → (inode, plain_hash)
}
```

**Promotion logic**:
- A directory starts with an empty `DirIndex` (`complete = false`).
- Each cold scan (`lookup` that misses the cache) increments `cold_scans`.
- After `DIR_INDEX_BUILD_AFTER_SCANS = 8` cold scans **or** on a **negative lookup** (name not found after full scan), the directory is fully indexed: `build_dir_index()` reads all blocks, populates `stored` and `plain` maps, sets `complete = true`, and caches `tail_offset`.
- Once `complete`, **both hits and misses are O(1)** via hash map lookup.

On **encrypted filesystems**, `stored` holds the ciphertext names (as stored on disk) while `plain` holds plaintext names → avoids re-encrypting during `list_dir` or re-lookup. On **unencrypted filesystems**, both maps are identical (plaintext = ciphertext).

### ShardedDirCache: 32-way concurrent cache

```rust
const NUM_DIR_CACHE_SHARDS: usize = 32;
type DirCacheShard = CachePadded<RwLock<FxHashMap<u64, DirIndex>>>;
```

<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../src/disk/caches.rs#L353-L395] file "../src/disk/caches.rs" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
The [`ShardedDirCache`](../src/disk/caches.rs#L353-L395) divides `dir_inode_id → DirIndex` across 32 independent `RwLock` shards using **64-bit Fibonacci hashing** (multiplicative bijection with `0x517cc1b727220a95`). This ensures:

- Cold indexing (`build_dir_index`), `list_dir` promotion, or `create_file`/`delete_file` cache maintenance on one directory **never stalls** concurrent `lookup`, `resolve_path`, or `list_dir` operations on other directories.
- Shard index computation: `(dir_inode_id.wrapping_mul(0x517cc1b727220a95) as usize) & 31` — single multiply + bitwise AND, no modulo.

Operations:
- `read_shard(dir_inode_id)` / `write_shard(dir_inode_id)` — acquire shard lock
- `remove(dir_inode_id)` — evicts index on directory deletion/rename
- `clear()` — drops all indices (format migration)
- `for_each_mut(f)` — iterates all indices (used for cache-wide invalidation)

---

## Filename Encryption

On encrypted filesystems, directory entries store **ciphertext filenames** (with `_e_` prefix) instead of plaintext. Encryption is **deterministic** (SIV construction) so identical names in the same parent directory produce identical ciphertext, enabling hash-based lookup on ciphertext.

### Encryption algorithm

```
encrypt_filename(key, parent_inode, name):
    1. Skip if name is "", ".", ".." (pass through plaintext)
    2. nonce = derive_filename_siv_nonce(key, parent_inode, name_bytes)
       // BLAKE2b-512("OIFS_SIV_FILENAME_V2_XCHACHA20" || filename_siv_key || parent_inode_le || name) → first 24 bytes
    3. aad = filename_aad_stack(parent_inode) // binds parent inode to AAD
    4. ciphertext = XChaCha20-Poly1305_encrypt(key.filename_cipher_key, nonce, aad, name)
    5. payload = [24-byte nonce | ciphertext | 16-byte Poly1305 tag]
    6. encoded = "_e_" + Base64URL_unpadded(payload)
    7. return encoded
```

**Key separation**: The master `EncryptionKey` derives two independent subkeys via HKDF:
- `filename_siv_key` → used only for SIV nonce derivation
- `filename_cipher_key` → used only for XChaCha20-Poly1305 encryption

**AAD binding**: `parent_inode` (8-byte LE) is included in Poly1305 AAD, so a ciphertext block cannot be transplanted to a different parent directory without authentication failure.

### Decryption with legacy fallback

```
decrypt_filename_authenticated(key, parent_inode, name, encryption_version):
    1. If not prefixed "_e_" → return plaintext unchanged
    2. Decode Base64URL → payload
    3. If payload_len ≥ 40 (24 nonce + ≥1 ciphertext + 16 tag):
         nonce = payload[0..24]
         ciphertext_with_tag = payload[24..]
         decrypted = XChaCha20-Poly1305_decrypt(key.filename_cipher_key, nonce, aad, ciphertext_with_tag)
         Verify SIV: derive_filename_siv_nonce(key, parent_inode, decrypted) == nonce (constant-time)
         If OK → return decrypted
    4. If encryption_version < ENCRYPTION_SCHEME_CONTEXT_BOUND:
         Try legacy v1 decrypt (12-byte ChaCha20-Poly1305, BLAKE2b-512 "OIFS_SIV_FILENAME_V1")
         Verify SIV similarly
    5. Return DecryptionFailed
```

**Constant-time SIV verification** uses `ct_eq_slice` to avoid timing side-channels on the nonce comparison.

---

## Cache Interactions

### Inode cache: BoundedInodeCache

- 32 shards, Second-Chance (Clock) eviction, capacity 2048 entries
- `get(inode_id)` → marks `referenced` bit (shared load, keeps cache line in Shared MESI state)
- `insert(inode_id, inode)` → evicts LRU unreferenced entry when shard full
- `remove(inode_id)` / `clear()` — invalidation on write/migration

### Payload caches

- **ChunkReadCache** (16 shards): Caches decompressed 64KB chunks for seekable files. Key = `(inode_id, chunk_idx, raw_entry, valid_len)`. Max 2 entries/shard.
- **DecodedBlobCache** (16 shards): Caches full decoded payloads for non-seekable compressed/encrypted files. Key = `(inode_id, size, compressed_size, first_block, nonce)`. Bounded by 32 MB total, 16 MB/entry.

### Directory cache: ShardedDirCache

As described above — 32 shards, `DirIndex` promotion after 8 cold scans or on negative lookup, O(1) lookups once complete, Fibonacci hashing for shard distribution.

---

## Summary of Key Invariants

| Invariant | Enforced by |
|-----------|-------------|
| Inode slot = exactly 256 bytes, zero-padded | `encode_v2()` / `INODE_SLOT_SIZE` |
| Frozen field offsets `[0..166)` never change | `INODE_V2_PAYLOAD_LEN`, Kani proof |
| CRC32C covers `[0..171)` when `record_version == 3` | `encode_v2_inner(stamp_v3_crc=true)` / `decode_v2()` |
| BlockPath decomposition is bijective and bounds-safe | `from_logical()` / `to_logical()` / Kani proofs |
| ChunkEntry bit fields are isolated | `new()` / accessors / Kani field isolation proof |
| DirIndex promotion: `cold_scans ≥ 8` ∨ negative lookup → `complete = true` | `build_dir_index()` logic in `DiskManager` |
| SipHash filter never causes false negatives | `check_hash_filter_soundness` Kani proof |
| Filename encryption binds `parent_inode` in AAD + SIV | `filename_aad_stack`, `derive_filename_siv_nonce` |
| Sharded caches never contend across unrelated inodes/dirs | 32-way Fibonacci sharding (`0x517cc1b727220a95`) |
