nodes.title: Superblock & On-Disk Layout
nodes.description: Comprehensive documentation of the OIFS superblock structure, format versioning (v1/v2/v3), block layout geometry, journal region placement, encryption fields, and migration cursor mechanics for in-place format upgrades.
nodes.body:
## Responsibility and ownership

The superblock subsystem ([`src/superblock.rs`](../../src/superblock.rs)) defines the foundational on-disk geometry and physical layout of an OIFS image.

The [`SuperBlock`](../../src/superblock.rs#L21-L72) resides at **Block 0** (byte offset `0..4096`) of the container image. It acts as the root configuration header, storing filesystem identification, block metrics, physical offsets to metadata regions (bitmaps and inode tables), encryption parameters, root directory references, and format versioning state.

## The SuperBlock structure

The [`SuperBlock`](../../src/superblock.rs#L21-L72) struct is marked `#[repr(C)]` for fixed binary alignment:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct SuperBlock {
    pub magic: u32,
    pub block_size: u32,
    pub block_count: u64,
    pub inode_bitmap_block: u64,
    pub data_bitmap_block: u64,
    pub inode_table_block: u64,
    pub inode_count: u64,
    pub data_block_start: u64,
    pub root_inode: u64,
    pub encrypted: bool,
    pub encryption_salt: [u8; 16],
    pub encryption_version: u8,
    pub format_version: u32,
    pub migration_cursor: u64,
}
```

### Magic identification

The filesystem is identified by a 4-byte magic number ([`SuperBlock::MAGIC = 0x4F494653`](../../src/superblock.rs#L77)), which corresponds to ASCII `"OIFS"` (`0x4F` = `'O'`, `0x49` = `'I'`, `0x46` = `'F'`, `0x53` = `'S'`). During `DiskManager::open`, any file lacking this exact magic returns `DiskManagerError::InvalidMagic`, rejecting non-OIFS binary files before attempting to interpret metadata.

### Field descriptions

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `magic` | Fixed value `0x4F494653` (`"OIFS"` in ASCII) used to validate the filesystem type. |
| `block_size` | Uniform filesystem block size in bytes (set to [`BLOCK_SIZE = 4096`](../../src/lib.rs#L17)). |
| `block_count` | Total physical block capacity of the container image (`file_size / 4096`). |
| `inode_bitmap_block` | Block ID where the inode bitmap starts (legacy: fixed Block `1`; v3: variable). |
| `data_bitmap_block` | Block ID where the data bitmap starts (legacy: fixed Block `2`; v3: variable). |
| `inode_table_block` | Block ID where the inode table starts (legacy/journaled: fixed; v3: calculated). |
| `inode_count` | Total number of allocated inode slots in the inode table. |
| `data_block_start` | First block number assigned for file and directory data payloads. |
| `root_inode` | Index of the root directory inode (always `0`). |
| `encrypted` | Boolean flag indicating if cryptographic AEAD encryption is active. |
| `encryption_salt` | 16-byte random salt used by Argon2id to derive the master key. |
| `encryption_version` | Cryptographic suite version (`1` = legacy XChaCha20-Poly1305 without AAD, `2` = context-bound with associated data). |
| `format_version` | On-disk format version. Determines the inode encoding layout and bitmap sizing strategy. Must remain the last field before `migration_cursor` to preserve backward compatibility. |
| `migration_cursor` | During format migration, indicates which inode IDs have been converted to the new format. Zero means no migration in progress. |

### Format versions

| Version | Constant | Meaning |
|---------|----------|---------|
| 0 (from zero padding) | — | Pre-versioning image; treated as legacy |
| 1 | `FORMAT_VERSION_LEGACY` | Legacy `bincode` inode encoding, single-block bitmaps |
| 2 | `FORMAT_VERSION_FIXED_INODE` | Fixed 256-byte inode records, single-block bitmaps |
| 3 | `FORMAT_VERSION_V3_LAYOUT` | **v3 layout** — multi-block bitmaps sized to image, 256-byte inode records, optional journal region |

The `format_version` field is **appended before `migration_cursor`** so that pre-versioning images (which lack this field entirely) decode with `format_version == 0` from zero padding, which correctly classifies them as legacy. Adding the field in the middle would shift every subsequent field and silently corrupt every existing image.

### Inode format dispatch

During a migration the superblock still advertises the legacy version so an interrupted migration stays readable, while slots below `migration_cursor` already hold current-format records:

```rust
pub fn inode_record_version_for(&self, inode_id: u64) -> u32 {
    if !self.is_legacy_inode_format() || inode_id < self.migration_cursor {
        Self::FORMAT_VERSION_FIXED_INODE
    } else {
        Self::FORMAT_VERSION_LEGACY
    }
}
```

This per-inode dispatch means a mixed-format image is **safe and resumable**, not corrupt.

---

## v3 Layout (format_version = 3)

The v3 layout introduces **multi-block bitmaps** sized to image capacity, removing the 128 MiB / 32K inode caps that constrained v1/v2. Bitmap spans are **implicit** in the recorded block offsets and validated by [`SuperBlock::validate()`](../../src/superblock.rs#L508-L588).

### Layout regions

The v3 metadata regions are laid out sequentially:

```
[superblock][inode bitmap: N][data bitmap: M][journal: J][inode table: T][data area]
```

Where:
- **Superblock**: Block 0 (always)
- **Inode bitmap**: Starts at Block 1, spans `N = ceil(inode_count / BITMAP_BLOCK_BITS)` blocks
- **Data bitmap**: Starts immediately after inode bitmap, spans `M = ceil(data_blocks / BITMAP_BLOCK_BITS)` blocks
- **Journal (optional)**: `J = JOURNAL_RESERVED_BLOCKS = 33` blocks (1 header + 32 ring) when `journaled=true`
- **Inode table**: Starts after data bitmap (and journal if present), spans `T` blocks (capped at 1024 blocks = 16,384 inodes at 256 bytes/record)
- **Data area**: Everything after the inode table

### Layout computation in `SuperBlock::new_v3`

The layout is computed in a **single pass** (no iterative fixed-point) to keep CBMC proofs tractable:

1. **Metadata overhead**: `1 (superblock) + inode_bitmap_blocks + 1 (data bitmap placeholder) + journal_blocks`
2. **Inode table**: Historical cap of 1024 blocks (16,384 inodes at 256 bytes/record). If space is tight, sized to ~25% of available space.
3. **Inode count**: `inode_table_blocks * INODE_SLOTS_PER_BLOCK` (where `INODE_SLOTS_PER_BLOCK = 4096 / 256 = 16`)
4. **Inode bitmap blocks**: `ceil(inode_count / BITMAP_BLOCK_BITS)`, minimum 1
5. **Data blocks**: Remaining blocks after all metadata
6. **Data bitmap blocks**: `ceil(data_blocks / BITMAP_BLOCK_BITS)`, minimum 1
6. **Block offsets**: Computed sequentially from the spans above

Minimum size: **5 blocks** for non-journaled; **37+ blocks** for journaled (requires 33-block WAL region).

### Key constants

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|----------|-------|---------|
| `BITMAP_BLOCK_BITS` | 32,768 | Bits per bitmap block (4096 × 8) |
| `MAX_TRACKED_INODES` | 32,768 | Maximum inodes the inode bitmap can track |
| `INODE_SLOTS_PER_BLOCK` | 16 | 256-byte inode records per 4096-byte block |
| `JOURNAL_RESERVED_BLOCKS` | 33 | 1 header + 32 ring blocks |
| `FORMAT_VERSION_V3_LAYOUT` | 3 | Format version marker |

---

## Journal Region Detection

Journal presence is detected **purely by geometry** — the `SuperBlock` struct is **identical** between journaled and non-journaled images. No extra flag is needed.

### Legacy/journaled (v1/v2 layout)

Fixed layout: inode table starts at block 36 (`JOURNAL_INODE_TABLE_BLOCK = 3 + 33`). Detected by:

```rust
pub fn is_journaled_layout(sb: &SuperBlock) -> bool {
    sb.inode_table_block >= JOURNAL_INODE_TABLE_BLOCK  // 36
}
```

### v3 layout (format_version ≥ 3)

Variable layout: journal region sits between data bitmap and inode table. Detected by:

```rust
pub fn has_journal_layout(&self) -> bool {
    if self.is_v3_layout() {
        let without_journal = 1 + self.inode_bitmap_blocks() + self.data_bitmap_blocks();
        self.inode_table_block == without_journal + crate::journal::JOURNAL_RESERVED_BLOCKS
    } else {
        crate::journal::is_journaled_layout(self)
    }
}
```

The journal header block is at `data_bitmap_block + data_bitmap_blocks()` and carries magic `JRNL` (`0x4A52_4E4C`).

---

## Superblock Validation

[`SuperBlock::validate(mmap_len)`](../../src/superblock.rs#L508-L588) enforces:

1. **Magic**: Must equal `0x4F494653`
2. **Block size**: Must equal 4096
3. **Minimum blocks**: ≥ 5 (≥ 37 for journaled via geometry)
4. **Bounds**: `block_count × 4096 ≤ mmap_len`
5. **Fixed offsets**: `inode_bitmap_block == 1`, `data_bitmap_block` after inode bitmap
6. **Ordering**: `inode_table_block > data_bitmap_block`, `inode_table_block ≤ data_block_start ≤ block_count`
7. **Inode count**: > 0, ≤ `MAX_TRACKED_INODES` (32,768)
8. **Table fit**: Usable inodes must fit between `inode_table_block` and `data_block_start`
9. **Root inode**: Must be < usable inode count
10. **Format version**: ≤ 3
11. **Migration cursor**: ≤ usable inode count
12. **Encryption consistency**: Version must match `encrypted` flag
13. **v3 geometry**: Bitmap spans must exactly match recorded offsets (implicit span validation)

---

## Format Migration (v1 → v2 → v3)

### Migration cursor mechanism

The [`migration_cursor`](../../src/superblock.rs#L72) enables **crash-safe, resumable in-place migration**:

- **Before migration**: `format_version = 1`, `migration_cursor = 0`
- **During migration**: `format_version = 1` (legacy), `migration_cursor` advances as inodes are rewritten
- **After migration**: `format_version = 3` (v3 layout), `migration_cursor = 0`

### Migration algorithm in `DiskManager::migrate`

1. **Checkpoint journal** first (prevents pending `WriteInode` ops in old format from corrupting rewritten slots)
2. **Snapshot inode bitmap** to know which slots are allocated
3. **For each inode from `cursor` to `inode_count`**:
   - If allocated: decode with v1 format, encode as v2 (256-byte fixed), write slot, flush
   - Advance `migration_cursor`, persist superblock, flush block 0
4. **On completion**: Set `format_version = 3`, clear `migration_cursor`, flush

### Per-inode version dispatch

Readers use [`inode_record_version_for(inode_id)`](../../src/superblock.rs#L110-L118) to decode the correct format per slot, making the intermediate mixed state **safe and readable**.

---

## In-Place Resize

The method [`in_place_block_count_range()`](../../src/superblock.rs#L354-L382) returns the `(min_blocks, max_blocks)` range where `block_count` can change **without relocating any metadata or data blocks**. The bitmap spans (`N`, `M`) and journal presence (`J`) remain invariant within this range.

For v3:
- `base = 1 + N + 1 + J + T`
- `max_blocks = base + M × BITMAP_BLOCK_BITS`
- `min_blocks` ensures the data bitmap doesn't shrink below its recorded span

---

## Encryption Fields

- `encrypted: bool` — master toggle
- `encryption_salt: [u8; 16]` — Argon2id salt for key derivation
- `encryption_version: u8` — 1 = legacy XChaCha20-Poly1305 (no AAD), 2 = context-bound (with AAD)

Validation rejects unknown versions or mismatched `encrypted`/`encryption_version` combinations.

---

## Related Pages

- [Block Allocation](block_allocation.md) — bitmap structure and allocation algorithms
- [Inode & Directory](inode_and_directory.md) — inode record formats (v1 bincode vs v2 fixed 256-byte)
- [Journal](journal.md) — WAL ring buffer, recovery, and journal region layout
- [Overview](overview.md) — high-level architecture

nodes.title: Configuration
nodes.description: Documents all configuration knobs: Cargo features, CLI flags, environment variables, session modes, compression modes, durability modes, auto-defrag, storage modes, and their interactions.
nodes.body:
OIFS provides multiple configuration mechanisms to tailor functionality for different use cases, from embedded systems to high-performance clusters. Configuration occurs at build time via Cargo features, at runtime via CLI flags and environment variables, and through persistent filesystem properties stored in the superblock.

## Build-Time Features

Optional functionality is controlled through Cargo features in `Cargo.toml`:

| Feature | Description | Default |
|---------|-------------|---------|
| `default` | Enables `cli` and `io_uring` features | Yes |
| `cli` | Builds the `oifs` CLI binary (requires `clap`) | Yes (via default) |
| `mcp` | Adds MCP (Model Context Protocol) server capabilities via the `oifs_mcp` binary; required for the `--network` / `-n` CLI flag | No |
| `io_uring` | Enables Linux io_uring backend for accelerated I/O (Linux-only, requires kernel ≥ 5.15 or RHEL 9.3+ backport) | Yes (via default, Linux-only) |
| `blosc2` | Enables native C-Blosc2 interop wrappers (`filters::blosc2_compress`/`blosc2_decompress`) | No |

**Encryption dependencies** (`chacha20poly1305`, `argon2`, `rand`, `zeroize`, `blake2`, `base64ct`) and **compression dependencies** (`zstd`, `rayon`) are always linked; they are not behind feature flags.

The `io_uring` feature is conditional: it only links the `io-uring` dependency on Linux targets (`cfg(target_os = "linux")`). On other platforms or when disabled, the io_uring backend compiles to nothing and falls back to `pread`.

## Runtime Configuration

### Environment Variables

| Variable | Purpose | Values |
|----------|---------|--------|
| `OIFS_IO_BACKEND` | Selects I/O backend for payload reads | `mmap`, `pread`, `io_uring` (aliases: `uring`, `iouring`, `io-uring`), case-insensitive |
| `OIFS_PASSWORD` | Provides password for encrypted filesystems | String (overridden by `--password` flag unless in `--json` mode) |
| `OIFS_ALLOW_PRE_5_15` | Allows io_uring on kernels older than 5.15 / RHEL 9.3 backport (Linux only) | Any non-empty value (e.g., `1`, `true`) |
| `OIFS_STORAGE_MODE` | Selects default storage mode for new/open images | `mmap`, `pread`, `file`, `file_io`, `no-mmap` (case-insensitive) |
| `OIFS_FILE_IO_CACHE_MB` | User-space data page cache budget for `StorageMode::FileIo` in MiB (`0` disables) | Integer, default `32`, max `4096` (4 GiB) |

#### I/O Backend Resolution

The I/O backend selection follows this precedence:

1. Explicit request via `DiskManager::set_io_backend(IoBackend)` (API)
2. `OIFS_IO_BACKEND` environment variable (parsed case-insensitively)
3. Default: `IoBackend::Mmap`

Requested backends that are unavailable (e.g., `io_uring` on non-Linux, `io_uring` feature disabled, kernel too old, `io_uring_disabled` sysctl, seccomp-filtered container) silently fall back to `IoBackend::Pread`. The actual backend in use can be queried via `IoBackend::resolve()`.

**Kernel version gating:** The io_uring backend requires Linux ≥ 5.15 or a RHEL 9.3+ backport (kernel `5.14.0-362+` with `.el9` in the release string). The check is enforced by `uring_supported()` in `src/io_engine.rs` unless `OIFS_ALLOW_PRE_5_15` is set in the environment.

#### Storage Mode Resolution

The storage mode selection follows this precedence:

1. Explicit request via `DiskManager::open_with_storage_mode()` or `set_default_storage_mode()` (API)
2. `OIFS_STORAGE_MODE` environment variable (parsed case-insensitively)
3. Default: `StorageMode::Mmap`

### CLI Flags

Global flags affecting all commands (defined in `src/bin/oifs.rs`):

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--image`, `-i <path>` | Path to OIFS image file |
| `--password <pwd>` | Password for encrypted filesystem (overrides `OIFS_PASSWORD`) |
| `--ipc` | Enable local IPC (Inter-Process Communication) mode for multi-process concurrency on the same machine (Unix Domain Socket in `/tmp`) |
| `--network`, `-n` | Enable cross-machine/network mode (for NFS, Lustre, or multi-node clusters); requires `mcp` feature |
| `--bind <addr>` | Custom bind address for network mode (e.g., `0.0.0.0:9050` or `127.0.0.1:0`) |
| `--allow-remote-ipc` | Allow the IPC master to bind a non-loopback address (required when using `--bind` with a non-loopback address; only safe when traffic is tunnelled via WireGuard, IPsec, SSH port forwarding) |
| `--json` | Output results as minified JSON (suppresses interactive password prompts) |
| `--auto-defrag[=THRESHOLD]` | Enable the background automatic defragmentation coordinator. Optional fragmentation threshold (0.0–1.0); defaults to 0.25. Ratio is `(free_runs - 1) / (free_blocks - 1)`. |
| `--defrag-interval <seconds>` | Interval in seconds between background fragmentation checks; defaults to 300 (minimum 10 ms enforced internally) |
| `--no-mmap` | Use pure positional `pread`/`pwrite` file I/O instead of mmap (eliminates `SIGBUS` and mmap hazards); sets `StorageMode::FileIo` |
| `--read-only` | Open the image in read-only mode (shared `F_RDLCK` lock, zero writes, works on 0444 images) |
| `--dict <path>` | Custom Zstd dictionary file(s) to register (first is also set as default compressor) |
| `--auto-grow[=MAX_MB]` | Automatically expand image capacity on block or inode exhaustion (optional hard cap in MiB, e.g. `--auto-grow` or `--auto-grow=64`) |

Command-specific configuration:

- `create`: `--size <MB>` (default 10), `--encrypt`, `--journal` (enables metadata WAL)
- `put`: `--compress`, `--no-compress`, `--chunked` (seekable 64KB chunked compression), `--filter <type>` (`none`, `delta`, `shuffle`, `bitshuffle`, `both`, `auto`), `--typesize <bytes>` (1, 2, 4, 8)
- `defrag`: `--mode <safe|inplace>` (default `safe`)

### Session Mode Selection

The session mode determines how processes coordinate access to the same image. It is selected via CLI flags or the `OifsSession` API:

| Mode | CLI Flag | API Method | Transport | Use Case |
|------|----------|------------|-----------|----------|
| `Standalone` | (none) | `get_or_open` | None (direct `mmap`) | Single process, zero overhead |
| `Local` | `--ipc` | `open_local` | Unix Domain Socket in `/tmp` | Multi-process on one machine |
| `Network` | `--network` / `-n` | `open_network` | TCP + rendezvous file (`.image.master`) | NFS, Lustre, multi-node clusters |

**Network mode requires the `mcp` feature** (it pulls in `tokio` and `rmcp`). The `oifs_mcp` binary also requires the `mcp` feature.

### Password Resolution

Encrypted filesystems require a password. Resolution precedence:

1. `--password` CLI flag
2. `OIFS_PASSWORD` environment variable
3. Interactive prompt (suppressed in `--json` mode to keep stdout pure for JSON pipelines)

The password is stored in a `Zeroizing<String>` buffer and wiped on drop.

## Persistent Filesystem Properties (Superblock)

The superblock (block 0) stores immutable and mutable filesystem properties that persist across mounts. Key feature flags and fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `encrypted` | `bool` | Whether the filesystem uses encryption |
| `encryption_version` | `u8` | Encryption scheme: `1` = legacy (XChaCha20-Poly1305 without AAD), `2` = context-bound (AAD binds ciphertext to inode/chunk) |
| `format_version` | `u32` | On-disk format: `1` = legacy bincode inodes, `2` = fixed 256-byte inodes (`INODE_FORMAT_V2`), `3` = v3 layout with multi-block bitmaps |
| `migration_cursor` | `u64` | In-place format migration progress cursor (0 = no migration) |
| Journal layout | Derived | Detected via `has_journal_layout()`: true when inode table starts after data bitmap + `JOURNAL_RESERVED_BLOCKS` (33 blocks: 1 header + 128 KB ring) |

**No `case_insensitive` or `chunked` flags exist in the superblock.** Case sensitivity is not a filesystem-level setting. Chunked compression is a per-write `CompressionMode::Seekable` choice, not a persistent property.

### Encryption Schemes

- **Legacy (`ENCRYPTION_SCHEME_LEGACY = 1`)**: XChaCha20-Poly1305 without associated data. Files can be swapped or rolled back without detection.
- **Context-bound (`ENCRYPTION_SCHEME_CONTEXT_BOUND = 2`)**: AEAD with associated data binding ciphertext to inode ID (and for chunks, to chunk index + flags). Prevents ciphertext relocation, reordering, and rollback attacks. New images use this scheme.

### Format Versions

- **v1 (Legacy)**: Packed `bincode` inode records. Read-only; existing images stay usable but keep writing v1 records until migrated.
- **v2 (Fixed Inode)**: 256-byte fixed-width inode records with explicit little-endian fields (`INODE_FORMAT_V2`).
- **v3 (Layout)**: Multi-block bitmaps that scale with image size (removes the 128 MiB / 32,768 block cap of v1/v2). `FORMAT_VERSION_V3_LAYOUT = 3`.

### Journaling

When `--journal` is passed to `create`, the superblock reserves 33 blocks (1 header + 128 KB ring) between the data bitmap and the inode table. Uncommitted transactions are replayed automatically on the next mount, making `fsck` unnecessary after power loss. The presence of the journal is detected by layout geometry, not a dedicated boolean flag.

## Compression Modes

`CompressionMode` (from `src/disk.rs`) controls when and how files are compressed:

| Mode | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| `Always` | Always compress, regardless of file size (stream mode) |
| `Never` | Never compress |
| `Auto` (default) | Compress files ≥ 8 KB |
| `Stream { level }` | Full-file stream compression with explicit Zstd level (1–19, 0 = default 3) |
| `Seekable { chunk_size, level }` | Seekable chunked compression with independent chunks (default 64 KB chunks, level 1 recommended) |

The `--chunked` CLI flag selects `Seekable { chunk_size: 64KB, level: 3 }`.

### Pre-compression Filters

Applied before Zstd to improve compression ratio on structured data:

| Filter | CLI `--filter` Value | Description |
|--------|---------------------|-------------|
| None | `none` | No filter |
| Delta | `delta` | First-order delta encoding (good for time-series, monotonic data) |
| Byte Shuffle | `shuffle` | Groups identical significance bytes (good for AoS structs) |
| Bit Shuffle | `bitshuffle` | Bit-level transpose (good for sparse bits, boolean masks) |
| Numeric (Delta + Shuffle) | `both` or `numeric` | Delta then byte shuffle |
| Auto | `auto` | Analyzes file content and selects best filter |

Element size (`--typesize`) controls filter granularity: 1, 2, 4, or 8 bytes (default 4).

## Durability Modes

`DurabilityMode` (from `src/disk.rs`) controls `msync` behavior:

| Mode | Value | Behavior |
|------|-------|----------|
| `Lazy` (default) | `0` | Mutations update shared mmap + OS page cache without per-mutation `msync`. Visible to all processes immediately; survives process crashes. Persistence across power loss guaranteed on explicit `flush()`, `Drop`, or kernel writeback. ~45x faster bulk writes. |
| `Full` | `1` | Each mutation issues `msync(MS_SYNC)`. Maximum power-loss resilience; slower. |

## Auto-Defragmentation

Background coordination configured via `--auto-defrag[=THRESHOLD]` and `--defrag-interval`:

- **Threshold** (default 0.25): Fragmentation ratio `(free_runs - 1) / (free_blocks - 1)`. 0.0 = fully contiguous, 1.0 = every free block isolated.
- **Interval** (default 300 s): Time between fragmentation checks (min 10 ms).
- Runs only on the IPC master (Standalone or master in Local/Network mode). Disabled in `--read-only` mode and on proxy (client) sessions.

## Storage Modes

`StorageMode` (from `src/storage.rs`) controls the file access strategy:

| Mode | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `Mmap` (default) | Memory-mapped I/O |
| `Pread` | Positional `pread`/`pwrite` |
| `FileIo` | User-space cached `pread`/`pwrite` with `OIFS_FILE_IO_CACHE_MB` budget |
| `NoMmap` | Alias for `FileIo` (set by `--no-mmap`) |

## Configuration Interactions

- `--no-mmap` overrides `OIFS_STORAGE_MODE` and sets `StorageMode::FileIo`.
- `--network` requires the `mcp` feature (build-time).
- `io_uring` backend requires Linux + `io_uring` feature + kernel ≥ 5.15 (or `OIFS_ALLOW_PRE_5_15`).
- `--auto-defrag` only takes effect on the master process; proxy sessions warn and ignore it.
- `--read-only` disables auto-defrag, auto-grow, and writes; opens with shared `F_RDLCK`.
- Encryption and compression are independent: encrypted files may still be compressed (compression runs before encryption).
- Password is required for `create --encrypt`, and for opening any encrypted image.

nodes.title: MCP Integration Guide
nodes.description: Guide to integrating AI agents and IDEs with OIFS via the Model Context Protocol server. Covers stdio transport, tool schemas, encrypted sandboxes, and client configuration.
nodes.body:
# MCP Integration Guide

This guide explains how to integrate AI agents and IDEs with the OIFS filesystem using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. The MCP server exposes OIFS as a set of tools that AI agents can use to read, write, and manage files within a sandboxed disk image.

## Running the MCP Server

The MCP server is provided as a standalone binary: `oifs_mcp`. It can be run directly with Cargo or installed via `cargo install`.

### Basic Usage

```bash
cargo run --bin oifs_mcp [IMAGE_PATH]
```

### Options

- `--size <MB>`: Set the initial size of the disk image when creating a new image (default: 10 MB).
- `-h, --help`: Show help message.

### Environment Variables

- `OIFS_PASSWORD`: If set, the disk image is opened (or created) as encrypted using this password. Required to open an existing encrypted image.

### Example

```bash
# Run with default image (agent_memory.img) and size (10 MB)
cargo run --bin oifs_mcp

# Run with custom image and size
cargo run --bin oifs_mcp -- --size 20 my_agent.img

# Run with encryption (requires OIFS_PASSWORD set)
OIFS_PASSWORD="secret" cargo run --bin oifs_mcp -- encrypted.img
```

The server communicates via stdio (standard input/output) and expects JSON-RPC 2.0 messages, making it compatible with any MCP client.

### Startup Behavior

1. **Image creation**: If the image file doesn't exist and `OIFS_PASSWORD` is set, `DiskManager::create_encrypted` is called. Otherwise `DiskManager::open_with_password` auto-creates a plain image.
2. **Size handling**: The `--size` value (megabytes) is multiplied by `1024 * 1024` with checked arithmetic to prevent silent overflow.
3. **Single image per process**: The CLI accepts exactly one positional image argument. All tools operate exclusively inside that image.
4. **Logging**: On startup the server logs to **stderr**: `[oifs-mcp] image=agent_memory.img size=10MB encrypted=false`.

### MCP Protocol Handshake

When an MCP client spawns the server, the following sequence occurs over stdio:

1. Client sends `initialize` request with protocol version and client info
2. Client sends `notifications/initialized` notification
3. Client calls `tools/list` to discover available tools
4. Subsequent `tools/call` invocations perform file operations

The server implements the MCP `ServerHandler` interface and advertises tool capabilities during initialization. It does **not** expose MCP resources (resource URIs, templates, or `resources/list`/`resources/read` handlers) — all filesystem access is mediated exclusively through the registered tools.

## Sandbox Isolation Model

Each `oifs_mcp` server instance operates on **exactly one disk image**. This creates a strong isolation boundary:

- **One image per server process** — All file operations are confined to the single `.img` file specified at startup.
- **No cross-image access** — An agent connected to one MCP server cannot access files in another agent's image.
- **Persistent state** — The disk image persists on disk. Reusing the same image path across sessions preserves agent memory.
- **Encryption per image** — When `OIFS_PASSWORD` is set, the entire image is encrypted with AES-256-XTS (with Argon2id key derivation). The same password must be provided to reopen it.

This model maps naturally to "one sandbox per agent session" or "one sandbox per project."

### Session Isolation for Multi-Tenant Use

The underlying `OifsSession` abstraction (in `src/session.rs`) provides three session modes that affect how multiple processes share an image:

| Mode | Transport | Use Case |
|------|-----------|----------|
| **Standalone** | Direct `mmap` — zero sockets, zero background threads | Single-process use (default for MCP server) |
| **Local IPC** | Unix Domain Socket in `/tmp` | Multi-process on the same machine |
| **Network** | TCP + rendezvous file (`.img.master`) | NFS/Lustre/shared storage, multi-node clusters |

The MCP server currently operates exclusively in **Standalone mode** (direct `mmap` access, zero IPC overhead). Each MCP server process gets its own `DiskManager` instance. For multi-tenant scenarios where multiple agents need isolated sandboxes, run separate `oifs_mcp` processes with different image paths. The process-wide session registry in `OifsSession` ensures that within a single process, multiple handles to the same canonicalized image path share one `DiskManager`.

**Authentication** for encrypted images is handled entirely via the `OIFS_PASSWORD` environment variable. The MCP server forwards this to `DiskManager`; it has no independent key-management logic. In IPC/Network modes, the Master process holds the encryption credentials and Proxies authenticate via a session secret or the password.

## Connecting from IDEs and AI Agents

The MCP server uses the **stdio transport** with **JSON-RPC 2.0**. Any MCP-compatible client can spawn the binary and communicate over stdin/stdout.

### Client Configuration: mcp.json

Both **Claude Desktop** and **Cursor** support an `mcp.json` (or `claude_desktop_config.json`) file to declare MCP servers. Add an entry for `oifs_mcp`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "oifs-sandbox": {
      "command": "oifs_mcp",
      "args": ["/absolute/path/to/agent_workspace.img", "--size", "64"],
      "env": {
        "OIFS_PASSWORD": "optional-vault-password"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

- **`command`**: Path to the `oifs_mcp` binary (must be on `PATH` or use absolute path).
- **`args`**: Positional arguments passed to the server. The first argument is the image path; `--size <MB>` sets initial size when creating a new image.
- **`env`**: Environment variables for the child process. Use `OIFS_PASSWORD` to enable encryption. Omit for an unencrypted image.

**Claude Desktop**: Place the config at `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` (macOS) or `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` (Windows).

**Cursor**: Place the config at `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (macOS/Linux) or `%USERPROFILE%\.cursor\mcp.json` (Windows).

Restart the IDE after editing the config file. The server will appear in the MCP servers list.

### Direct JSON-RPC Testing

You can test the server manually by piping JSON-RPC requests to its stdin:

```bash
echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"test","version":"1"}}}' | ./target/release/oifs_mcp --size 10 test.img
```

## Available MCP Tools

The server registers **eight tools** via `rmcp`'s `#[tool_router]` macro. Every tool:

- Clones the `DiskManager`
- Executes the operation inside `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` (bridging async `rmcp` to sync mmap I/O)
- Returns a **JSON string** built with `serde_json` (never hand-rolled `format!`) to guarantee correct escaping

### Response Convention

- **Success**: `{"ok": true, ...}` with tool-specific fields.
- **Failure**: `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}`.

### Tool Reference

| Tool | Description | Parameters |
|------|-------------|------------|
| `write_file` | Create or overwrite a file. Parent directories must already exist. | `path: string`, `content: string` |
| `read_file` | Read a file's contents as UTF-8 text. | `path: string` |
| `list_dir` | List entries at a path. Returns **JSON Lines (JSONL)** — one JSON object per line. | `path: string` (e.g., `"."` for root) |
| `mkdir` | Create a directory. Parent directories must exist (no `mkdir -p`). | `path: string` |
| `delete_file` | Delete a file. | `path: string` |
| `truncate_file` | Truncate or extend a file to a specific byte size. | `path: string`, `size: number` (bytes) |
| `append_file` | Append a line to a file (creates file if missing). Auto-adds trailing newline. Ideal for **JSONL memory logs**. | `path: string`, `content: string` |
| `status` | Show filesystem stats: image path, total/used/free blocks, fragmentation ratio. | *(none)* |

### Path Semantics

- All paths are **relative to the image root** (inode 1). There is no working-directory concept.
- Paths like `"notes/todo.txt"` or `"."` are resolved by `DiskManager::resolve_path` starting from root.
- `write_file`, `mkdir`, and `append_file` use `resolve_parent` to locate the parent directory inode, then create the child. They **do not** auto-create intermediate directories — the agent must call `mkdir` for each level first.
- Path components are not URL-encoded; they are used as raw directory entry names.

### `list_dir` JSONL Output

`list_dir` returns **one JSON object per line** (not a JSON array):

```json
{"name":"notes","kind":"dir","size":0}
{"name":"logs","kind":"dir","size":0}
{"name":"hello.txt","kind":"file","size":13}
```

This streaming-friendly format lets an agent process large directories incrementally.

## Resource URI Scheme: `oifs://<image>/<path>`

**Note**: The current `oifs_mcp` implementation does **not** expose MCP resources (the `resources/list` and `resources/read` handlers are not implemented). All filesystem access goes through tools only.

If future versions add resource support, the URI scheme would follow the pattern:

```
oifs://<image-name>/<path-inside-image>
```

Where `<image-name>` is the base filename of the `.img` file (e.g., `agent_memory`), and `<path-inside-image>` is the path relative to the image root (e.g., `notes/todo.txt`).

## Tool Allowlists and Sandbox Directory Restrictions

The MCP server does **not** implement a configurable tool allowlist or directory-level permissions within the sandbox. The sandbox boundary is the **entire disk image**:

- All eight tools are always available when the server starts.
- There is no mechanism to disable specific tools per-client.
- There is no path-prefix restriction inside the image — any path under the image root is accessible.

To achieve finer-grained isolation, run **separate `oifs_mcp` processes** with **different image files** per agent/project. Each process provides a completely independent filesystem with its own tool namespace.

## Typical Agent Loop

A common memory pattern for an agent across a conversation:

```text
1. write_file  →  create/overwrite a structured note (e.g., "context/project_plan.md")
2. append_file →  stream JSONL observations to a log (e.g., "logs/memory.jsonl")
3. list_dir    →  browse the sandbox to discover what exists (JSONL output)
4. read_file   →  recall a specific note or log file
```

Because the `.img` file persists on disk, **the same image path reused in a later session restores all files**. The agent's memory survives process restarts, host restarts, and machine reboots.

### Example: JSONL Log with `append_file`

**Request:**
```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":10,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"append_file","arguments":{"path":"logs/memory.jsonl","content":"{\"event\":\"observation\",\"ts\":1720000000,\"data\":{\"key\":\"value\"}}"}}}
```

**Response (success):**
```json
{"ok":true,"inode":42,"total_bytes":1024}
```

Each call appends one line (the tool auto-adds `\n` if missing). The resulting `logs/memory.jsonl` is valid JSONL — one complete JSON object per line — ready for streaming parsers.

## Encrypted Sandbox Workflow

1. **Set the password** in the host environment (or in the MCP client config `env` section):
   ```bash
   export OIFS_PASSWORD="strong-passphrase"
   ```
2. **Launch the server** (first run creates the encrypted image):
   ```bash
   ./target/release/oifs_mcp --size 50 agent_memory.img
   ```
   Startup log shows `encrypted=true`.
3. **Reopen later** — the same `OIFS_PASSWORD` must be present in the environment, otherwise `DiskManager::open_with_password` returns `PasswordRequired`.

The encryption is **image-scoped**: the entire `.img` file (superblock, inode table, data blocks, directory entries, filenames) is encrypted. Filenames use AES-SIV (deterministic authenticated encryption) so directory listings don't leak name lengths.

## Concurrency Model

`OifsMcpServer` holds `DiskManager` directly (not behind a `TokioMutex` — each blocking task gets its own clone, and `DiskManager` uses internal `RwLock`/`Mutex` for synchronization). An additional `append_lock: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<()>>` serializes concurrent `append_file` calls so that multiple agents appending to the same log file interleave cleanly line-by-line.

### Why This Is Acceptable for Agent Workloads

- **MCP over stdio is inherently sequential** from a single agent's perspective: an LLM emits one tool call, waits for the result, then emits the next.
- **No fan-out from a single host** — the stdio transport pairs one stdin/stdout with one server process. Concurrent access would only occur if multiple agent hosts connected to the same process, which the transport prevents by design.
- **Throughput implication**: The async–sync bridge adds negligible latency (microseconds) per tool call. For workloads requiring true parallelism (e.g., batch indexing, multi-agent coordination), the IPC/daemon path (`src/ipc.rs`) provides a multi-threaded alternative with a dedicated master process.

## Related Pages

- [MCP Server Architecture](../architecture/mcp_server.md) — internal structure, `rmcp` integration, tool registration.
- [MCP Workflow](../workflows/mcp_workflow.md) — detailed tool usage patterns and examples.
- [Quickstart](../quickstart.md) — building and running the MCP server.
- [Encrypted Workflows](../workflows/encrypted_workflows.md) — Argon2id parameters, key hierarchy, IPC authentication.

nodes.description: Complete reference for the oifs and oifs_mcp CLI commands: global flags, subcommands, arguments, JSON output, and exit codes.
nodes.body:
## Overview

The OIFS project provides two command-line executables:

| Binary | Source | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `oifs` | [`src/bin/oifs.rs`](../../src/bin/oifs.rs) | Full-featured CLI for creating, inspecting, modifying, and diagnosing OIFS filesystem images. |
| `oifs_mcp` | [`src/bin/oifs_mcp.rs`](../../src/bin/oifs_mcp.rs) | MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that exposes OIFS as tools for AI agents via stdio. |

Both binaries are built with [`clap`](https://crates.io/crates/clap) using the derive pattern. The `oifs` CLI routes operations through the [`OifsSession`](../architecture/overview.md) layer, meaning CLI commands automatically participate in multi-process Master-Proxy concurrency when IPC is enabled.

---

## `oifs` — Complete Command Reference

### Global Options

Global options apply across all subcommands and must appear **before** the subcommand:

| Flag | Long Option | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `-i` | `--image <PATH>` | Path to the target `.img` container file (required for all image commands except `filter-analyze` and `clone`). |
| `-p` | `--password <STR>` | Passphrase for encrypted images. **Highest precedence** in password resolution. |
| | `--ipc` | Enables local IPC (Unix Domain Sockets) mode for multi-process concurrency on the same machine. |
| `-n` | `--network` | Enables cross-machine Network TCP mode (for NFS, Lustre, multi-node clusters). Implies network mode if `--bind` is also set. |
| | `--bind <ADDR>` | Custom host:port to bind in network mode (e.g., `0.0.0.0:9050` or `127.0.0.1:0`). |
| | `--allow-remote-ipc` | Allow the IPC master to bind a non-loopback address. **Only safe when traffic is tunnelled** (WireGuard, IPsec, SSH port forwarding); the IPC transport is plain TCP without TLS. |
| | `--json` | Formats all command outputs as structured JSON and **disables interactive stdin prompts**. |
| | `--auto-defrag [THRESHOLD]` | Enable background automatic defragmentation coordinator. Optional fragmentation threshold (ratio of `(free_runs - 1) / (free_blocks - 1)`) above which a defragmentation pass is triggered. Default: `0.25`. Range: `0.0` (all free space contiguous) to `1.0` (every free block isolated). |
| | `--defrag-interval <SECONDS>` | Interval in seconds between background fragmentation checks. Default: `300` (5 minutes). Minimum: `1`. |
| | `--no-mmap` | Use pure positional `pread`/`pwrite` file I/O instead of `mmap` (eliminates SIGBUS and mmap hazards on network filesystems). |
| | `--read-only` | Open the image in read-only mode (shared `F_RDLCK` lock, zero writes, works on `0444` images). |
| | `--dict <PATH>` | Custom Zstd dictionary file(s) to register (first is also set as default compressor). Can be specified multiple times. |
| | `--auto-grow[=MAX_MB]` | Automatically expand image capacity on block or inode exhaustion (optional hard cap in MiB, e.g. `--auto-grow` or `--auto-grow=64`). Requires `=` when specifying a value. |
| `-h` | `--help` | Prints help information. |
| `-V` | `--version` | Prints version. |

### Password Resolution (3-Tier Hierarchy)

When interacting with encrypted filesystems, `oifs` determines passphrases according to a strict precedence hierarchy ([`src/bin/oifs.rs#L307-L342`](../../src/bin/oifs.rs#L307-L342)):

```
1. CLI Argument (--password <PWD>)
       │ (Present?) ── Yes ──> Use CLI argument
       No
2. Environment Variable (OIFS_PASSWORD)
       │ (Present?) ── Yes ──> Use environment variable
       No
3. Execution Mode Check (--json)
       ├── Enabled  ──> Abort immediately with JSON error
       └── Disabled ──> Secure Interactive Terminal Prompt (libc::termios)
```

1. **CLI Flag (`--password <pwd>`)**: Highest precedence. Useful for scripts and automated integration tests.
2. **Environment Variable (`OIFS_PASSWORD`)**: Preferred for CI/CD environments and background jobs to prevent secrets from appearing in `ps aux` process tables.
3. **Interactive Masked Prompt**: If neither flag nor environment variable is provided, `read_password` ([`src/bin/oifs.rs#L218-L256`](../../src/bin/oifs.rs#L218-L256)) disables terminal echo (`libc::ECHO`) via `libc::tcgetattr` / `libc::tcsetattr`, safely reading the password while masking input. Prompts are printed to `stderr` so stdout remains clean for shell pipes.
4. **Non-Interactive `--json` Enforcement**: In `--json` mode, interactive prompts are forbidden. If an encrypted image is opened without `--password` or `OIFS_PASSWORD`, the process immediately aborts with:
   ```json
   {"ok": false, "error": "Encrypted filesystem requires --password or OIFS_PASSWORD env in --json mode"}
   ```

**Password confirmation on creation** (`oifs -i disk.img create --encrypt`):
- Interactive mode prompts twice (`Enter password: ` and `Confirm password: `) to prevent accidental typos.
- If the password is fewer than 8 characters, a non-blocking warning is emitted to stderr: `⚠️ Warning: Password is shorter than 8 characters`.

---

### JSON Output Mode (`--json`)

The `--json` flag guarantees machine-readable outputs for automation, AI agent tools, and monitoring scripts:

- **Success Responses**: Emits JSON objects (e.g., `{"ok": true, "message": "..."}`) or formatted diagnostic reports.
- **Failure Responses**: Intercepts panics and errors in `main` ([`src/bin/oifs.rs#L358-L364`](../../src/bin/oifs.rs#L358-L364)), emitting `{"ok": false, "error": "<msg>"}` to stdout and exiting with status code 1.

#### Common JSON Success Schemas

| Subcommand | Success Schema | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `create` | `{"ok": true, "message": "Filesystem created", "journal": boolean}` | `journal` true if `--journal` was specified |
| `put` | `{"ok": true, "inode": <u64>, "bytes": <usize>}` | |
| `get` | `{"ok": true, "bytes": <usize>, "dest": "<path>"}` | |
| `cat` | `{"ok": true, "path": "<name>", "bytes": <usize>, "content": "<utf8_lossy>"}` | |
| `append` | `{"ok": true, "inode": <u64>, "total_bytes": <usize>}` | |
| `mkdir` | `{"ok": true, "inode": <u64>}` | |
| `rm` | `{"ok": true, "removed": "<path>", "inode": <u64>, "recursive": boolean}` | |
| `ls` | `[{"name": "...", "kind": "f\|d", "size": <u64>, "comp_size": <u64\|null>, "modified": "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"}, ...]` | Array of entries |
| `stat` | `{"ok": true, "path": "...", "inode": <u64>, "kind": "file\|directory", "size": <u64>, "compressed_size": <u64>, "encrypted": <bool>, "seekable_64k": <bool>, "created": "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS", "modified": "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"}` | |
| `info` | `{"ok": true, "image": "...", "block_size": <u32>, "block_count": <u64>, "total_bytes": <u64>, "inode_count": <u64>, "data_block_start": <u64>, "format_version": <u32>, "encrypted": <bool>, "journaled": <bool>, "read_only": <bool>}` | |
| `analyze` | `{"ok": true, "total_blocks": <u64>, "used_blocks": <u64>, "free_blocks": <u64>, "free_runs": <u64>, "largest_free_run": <u64>, "avg_gap_size": <f64>, "fragmentation_ratio": <f64>}` | |
| `defrag` | `{"ok": true, "files_processed": <u64>, "bytes_moved": <u64>, "frag_before": <f64>, "frag_after": <f64>}` | |
| `fsck` | Full `IntegrityReport` (see [fsck workflow](../workflows/fsck_workflow.md)) | |
| `migrate` | `{"ok": true, "from_version": <u32>, "to_version": <u32>, "inodes_rewritten": <u64>, "already_current": boolean}` | |
| `truncate` | `{"ok": true, "path": "<path>", "size": <u64>}` | |
| `mount` | `{"ok": true, "backend": "nfs\|fuse", "mountpoint": "...", "read_only": <bool>, "foreground": <bool>, "allow_other": <bool>}` | |
| `clone` | `{"ok": true, "src": "...", "dst": "...", "method": "..."}` | Method reflects OS CoW reflink type |
| `transfer` | See [Transfer JSON](#transfer-json-schemas) below | |
| `filter-analyze` | Pretty-printed `FilterRecommendation` (see below) | |
| `dict train` | `{"ok": true, "dict_id": <u32>, "bytes": <usize>, "output": "..."}` | |
| `resize` | `{"ok": true, "bytes_before": <u64>, "bytes_after": <u64>, "blocks_before": <u64>, "blocks_after": <u64>, "inodes_before": <u64>, "inodes_after": <u64>, "method": "..."}` | |
| `vacuum` | `{"ok": true, "bytes_before": <u64>, "bytes_after": <u64>, "bytes_reclaimed": <u64>, "blocks_before": <u64>, "blocks_after": <u64>, "blocks_relocated": <u64>, "method": "..."}` | |
| Error (any) | `{"ok": false, "error": "<message>"}` | Exit code 1 |

---

### Subcommands

#### `create` — Create a new OIFS image

```bash
oifs -i <image.img> create [--size <MB>] [--encrypt] [--journal]
```

| Option | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `--size <MB>` | Size in megabytes (default: 10). |
| `--encrypt` | Enable encryption (will prompt for password via 3-tier hierarchy). |
| `--journal` | Enable the metadata WAL (journaling) for crash-safe metadata updates. Reserves 33 blocks (1 header + 128 KB ring) between the data bitmap and the inode table. Uncommitted transactions are replayed automatically on the next mount, so `oifs fsck` is no longer needed after a power loss. |

**JSON success**: `{"ok": true, "message": "Filesystem created", "journal": true}`

---

#### `put` — Import a file into the image

```bash
oifs -i <image.img> put <host_path> [remote_name] [--compress] [--no-compress] [--chunked] [--filter <mode>] [--typesize <N>]
```

| Argument / Option | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `host_path` | File path on host (required). |
| `remote_name` | Destination filename in OIFS (optional, defaults to host filename). |
| `--compress` | Always compress the file regardless of size. |
| `--no-compress` | Never compress the file. |
| `--chunked` / `--seekable` / `--chunked-64k` | Seekable 64KB chunked compression (sets `INODE_FLAG_SEEKABLE_64K`). |
| `--filter <mode>` | Pre-compression filter: `none`, `delta`, `shuffle`, `bitshuffle`, `both` (alias `numeric`), or `auto`. Default: `none`. |
| `--typesize <N>` | Element size in bytes for filter (1, 2, 4, 8). Default: 0 (auto = 4). |

**Compression mode precedence**: `--chunked` > `--compress` > `--no-compress` > `Auto`.

**Filter modes**:
- `none` — No pre-filter.
- `delta` — First-order delta (good for time-series, linear data).
- `shuffle` — Byte shuffle (good for AoS struct arrays).
- `bitshuffle` — Bit-level transpose (good for boolean masks, sparse bits).
- `both` / `numeric` — Delta + byte shuffle (good for numeric arrays).
- `auto` — Analyze file content and recommend optimal filter.

**JSON success**: `{"ok": true, "inode": <u64>, "bytes": <usize>}`

---

#### `filter-analyze` — Analyze a file and recommend optimal compression filters

```bash
oifs filter-analyze <host_path> [--json]
```

Analyzes a host file (no image required) and prints a detailed filter recommendation report including entropy measurements, compression ratios, and the exact `oifs put` command to use.

**JSON output**: Pretty-printed `FilterRecommendation` struct with fields:
- `original_size`, `baseline_compressed_size`, `baseline_entropy`
- `candidates[]` with `label`, `entropy`, `compressed_size`, `compression_ratio`, `space_savings_percent`
- `best_config` — the recommended `FilterConfig`

---

#### `get` — Export a file from the image

```bash
oifs -i <image.img> get <remote_name> [host_path]
```

| Argument | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `remote_name` | Filename in OIFS (required). |
| `host_path` | Destination path on host (optional, defaults to remote filename). If host_path is a directory or ends with `/`, the remote filename is appended. |

**JSON success**: `{"ok": true, "bytes": <usize>, "dest": "<resolved_path>"}`

---

#### `cat` — Print file contents to stdout

```bash
oifs -i <image.img> cat <remote_name>
```

| Argument | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `remote_name` | Filename in OIFS (required). |

**Behavior**: Writes raw bytes to stdout (no newline added). In `--json` mode, returns a JSON object with the content as UTF-8 lossy string.

**JSON success**: `{"ok": true, "path": "...", "bytes": <usize>, "content": "<utf8_lossy>"}`

---

#### `info` — Display filesystem superblock and configuration

```bash
oifs -i <image.img> info
```

Shows block size, total blocks/bytes, inode capacity, format version, encryption status, journaling status, and read-only state.

---

#### `stat` — Display inode metadata for a file or directory

```bash
oifs -i <image.img> stat <path>
```

| Argument | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `path` | Path in OIFS (required). Use `/` for root directory. |

Shows inode number, type (file/directory), size, compressed size, encryption flag, seekable-64k flag, created/modified timestamps.

---

#### `append` — Append content to a file in the image

```bash
oifs -i <image.img> append <remote_name> <content> [--no-newline]
```

| Argument / Option | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `remote_name` | Destination filename in OIFS (creates if not exists). |
| `content` | Content to append (required). |
| `--no-newline` | Do not append a newline automatically if content doesn't end with one. |

**JSON success**: `{"ok": true, "inode": <u64>, "total_bytes": <usize>}`

---

#### `mkdir` — Create a directory

```bash
oifs -i <image.img> mkdir <dir_name>
```

| Argument | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `dir_name` | Directory name/path (parent must exist). |

**JSON success**: `{"ok": true, "inode": <u64>}`

---

#### `rm` — Delete a file or directory

```bash
oifs -i <image.img> rm <path> [-r|--recursive]
```

| Argument / Option | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `path` | Path of the file or directory to delete. |
| `-r`, `--recursive` | Allow deleting a directory that still has contents. |

**Safety**: Never allows deleting the filesystem root. Non-empty directories require `--recursive`.

**JSON success**: `{"ok": true, "removed": "<path>", "inode": <u64>, "recursive": <bool>}`

---

#### `ls` — List files in the root directory or specified path

```bash
oifs -i <image.img> ls [path] [-r|--recursive]
```

| Argument / Option | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `path` | Path to list (optional, defaults to root). |
| `-r`, `--recursive` | List recursively. |

**Output columns** (non-JSON): `Type`, `Name`, `Size`, `CompSize`, `Modified`. Type: `d` = directory, `-` = file.

**JSON success**: Array of entry objects (see [JSON schemas](#common-json-success-schemas)).

---

#### `analyze` — Analyze disk fragmentation

```bash
oifs -i <image.img> analyze
```

Reports total/used/free blocks, free runs (gaps), largest free run, average gap size, and fragmentation ratio.

---

#### `defrag` — Defragment the filesystem

```bash
oifs -i <image.img> defrag [--mode <safe|inplace>]
```

| Option | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `--mode <safe|inplace>` | Defragmentation mode (default: `safe`). `safe` uses copy-on-write; `inplace` modifies the image directly (⚠️ data loss risk if interrupted). |

**JSON success**: `{"ok": true, "files_processed": <u64>, "bytes_moved": <u64>, "frag_before": <f64>, "frag_after": <f64>}`

---

#### `fsck` — Check filesystem structural consistency

```bash
oifs -i <image.img> fsck
```

Performs a full structural integrity check: orphan inodes, leaked blocks, missing blocks, cross-linked blocks. Returns non-zero exit code if corruption is found.

**JSON output**: Full `IntegrityReport` object with `is_clean` boolean and arrays of issue IDs.

---

#### `migrate` — Upgrade a legacy image to current inode format

```bash
oifs -i <image.img> migrate
```

Upgrades legacy v1 inode format to current fixed-width format. Resumes interrupted migrations automatically.

**JSON success**: `{"ok": true, "from_version": <u32>, "to_version": <u32>, "inodes_rewritten": <u64>, "already_current": <bool>}`

---

#### `truncate` — Truncate or extend a file to specified size

```bash
oifs -i <image.img> truncate <path> --size <bytes>
```

| Argument / Option | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `path` | Remote path in OIFS. |
| `-s`, `--size <bytes>` | New size in bytes (required). |

**JSON success**: `{"ok": true, "path": "<path>", "size": <u64>}`

---

#### `mount` — Mount the OIFS image as a FUSE/NFS filesystem

```bash
oifs -i <image.img> mount <mountpoint> [--backend <auto|nfs|fuse>] [--port <N>] [--foreground] [--allow-other]
```

| Argument / Option | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `mountpoint` | Directory where the filesystem will be mounted (required). |
| `--backend` | Mount backend: `auto` (macOS: nfs, Linux: fuse), `nfs` (built-in local NFSv3, zero kext), or `fuse`. Default: `auto`. |
| `--port` | Loopback TCP port for NFSv3 backend (0 = OS-assigned ephemeral port). Default: 0. |
| `--foreground` | Run attached in the foreground and log mount details to stderr. |
| `--allow-other` | Allow other users to access the mounted filesystem (`allow_other`, FUSE backend only). |

**Read-only behavior**: If the image was opened with `--read-only` or the filesystem is read-only, the mount is read-only regardless of backend options.

**JSON success**: `{"ok": true, "backend": "nfs\|fuse", "mountpoint": "...", "read_only": <bool>, "foreground": <bool>, "allow_other": <bool>}`

---

#### `clone` — Clone an entire OIFS image using OS CoW reflink

```bash
oifs clone <src> <dst>
```

| Argument | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `src` | Source OIFS image path (defaults to `--image` if omitted). |
| `dst` | Destination OIFS image path (must not already exist). |

Uses `APFS clonefile` (macOS) or `FICLONE` (Linux) for instant copy-on-write clones.

**JSON success**: `{"ok": true, "src": "...", "dst": "...", "method": "..."}`

---

#### `transfer` — Fast cross-image file copy or move

```bash
oifs -i <src.img> transfer --to <dst.img> <src_path> [--dest <dst_path>] [--move] [--overwrite] [--to-password <pwd>] [--offset <N>] [--len <N>] [--dst-offset <N>] [--trim-mode <keep|punch-hole|collapse>]
```

**Three-tier transfer mechanism** (Direct sessions only):
1. **FICLONERANGE** — OS reflink for aligned extents (zero-copy).
2. **copy_file_range** — Kernel copy without user-space roundtrip.
3. **Raw block copy** — Direct block-level copy (bypasses decompression/recompression).

Falls back to logical re-encode (read + write) if either session is a Remote IPC proxy.

| Argument / Option | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `--to <PATH>` | Destination OIFS image path (required). |
| `src_path` | Source file path inside the source image (required). |
| `--dest <PATH>` | Destination file path inside `--to` image (defaults to `src_path`). |
| `--move` | Remove source file after destination commits and flushes. |
| `--overwrite` | Overwrite existing file at destination. |
| `--to-password <PWD>` | Password for encrypted destination image (optional). |
| `--offset <N>` | Sub-range byte offset in source file (enables `splice_range_to`). |
| `--len <N>` | Sub-range byte length to splice (defaults to remaining source bytes from `--offset`). |
| `--dst-offset <N>` | Sub-range byte offset in destination file (defaults to `--offset` or 0). |
| `--trim-mode <MODE>` | Source trim mode for sub-range splice: `keep` (default), `punch-hole`, `collapse`. |

##### Transfer JSON Schemas

**Full file transfer**:
```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "src_inode": <u64>,
  "dst_inode": <u64>,
  "logical_bytes": <u64>,
  "physical_bytes": <u64>,
  "extents_transferred": <usize>,
  "method": "Ficlonerange|CopyFileRange|RawBlockCopy|LogicalReencode",
  "moved": <bool>
}
```

**Sub-range splice transfer**:
```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "src_inode": <u64>,
  "dst_inode": <u64>,
  "bytes_spliced": <u64>,
  "logical_rmw_bytes": <u64>,
  "body_fast_path_bytes": <u64>,
  "physical_bytes": <u64>,
  "extents_transferred": <u64>,
  "src_blocks_freed": <u64>,
  "method": "Ficlonerange|CopyFileRange|RawBlockCopy|LogicalReencode",
  "trim_mode": "keep|punch-hole|collapse"
}
```

---

#### `dict` — Zstd dictionary utilities

```bash
oifs -i <image.img> dict train [--dir <path>] --output <dict_path> [--max-size <bytes>] [--max-samples <N>]
```

| Subcommand | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `train` | Train a Zstd dictionary from sample files stored inside an OIFS directory. |

**`train` options**:
| Option | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `--dir <path>` | Directory path inside the image (e.g. "/" or "/logs"). Default: `/`. |
| `-o`, `--output <PATH>` | Host output path for the trained Zstd dictionary (required). |
| `--max-size <bytes>` | Target dictionary size in bytes (256..=16777216). Default: 112640. |
| `--max-samples <N>` | Maximum number of regular files sampled from `--dir`. Default: 256. |

**JSON success**: `{"ok": true, "dict_id": <u32>, "bytes": <usize>, "output": "..."}`

---

#### `resize` — Resize (grow or shrink) an OIFS image container

```bash
oifs -i <image.img> resize [--size <MiB> | --bytes <N>]
```

| Option | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `--size <MiB>` | New target image size in MiB. |
| `--bytes <N>` | New target image size in exact bytes (rounded up to 4 KiB blocks). |

**Mutually exclusive**: `--size` and `--bytes` cannot be used together. One is required.

**JSON success**: `{"ok": true, "bytes_before": <u64>, "bytes_after": <u64>, "blocks_before": <u64>, "blocks_after": <u64>, "inodes_before": <u64>, "inodes_after": <u64>, "method": "..."}`

---

#### `vacuum` — Compact used blocks and shrink the image to reclaim unused space

```bash
oifs -i <image.img> vacuum [--headroom-mb <N>] [--headroom-pct <N>] [--min-size-mb <N>] [--no-relayout]
```

| Option | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `--headroom-mb <N>` | Minimum free headroom to retain in MiB (default: 1). |
| `--headroom-pct <N>` | Free headroom percentage relative to used data blocks 0..=100 (default: 15). |
| `--min-size-mb <N>` | Minimum image size floor in MiB (0 = no floor, default: 0). |
| `--no-relayout` | Disallow atomic cross-boundary re-layout (in-place shrink only). |

**JSON success**: `{"ok": true, "bytes_before": <u64>, "bytes_after": <u64>, "bytes_reclaimed": <u64>, "blocks_before": <u64>, "blocks_after": <u64>, "blocks_relocated": <u64>, "method": "..."}`

---

### Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| `0` | Success. |
| `1` | General error (invalid arguments, I/O error, filesystem corruption, etc.). In `--json` mode, error details are printed to stdout as `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}`. |

---

### Error Message Conventions

- **Human mode** (default): Errors printed to `stderr` with `Error: ` prefix. Warnings/notes printed to `stderr` without prefix (e.g., `⚠️ Warning: ...`, `✅ Created...`).
- **JSON mode** (`--json`): All output to `stdout` as JSON. Errors are `{"ok": false, "error": "<message>"}`. Interactive prompts are **suppressed**; missing passwords for encrypted images cause immediate abort with JSON error.
- **Panic handling**: `main` wraps `run_cli` and catches any error, ensuring JSON error format in `--json` mode.

---

## `oifs_mcp` — MCP Server Reference

The `oifs_mcp` binary runs as an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server over stdio, exposing OIFS filesystem operations as tools for AI agents (Cursor, Claude Desktop, etc.).

### Usage

```bash
oifs_mcp [--size <MB>] [IMAGE_PATH]
```

| Option / Argument | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `--size <MB>` | Initial size when creating a new image (default: 10 MB). |
| `IMAGE_PATH` | Path to the OIFS image file (default: `agent_memory.img`). |
| `-h`, `--help` | Show usage. |

### Environment

| Variable | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `OIFS_PASSWORD` | If set, opens (or creates) the image as encrypted. Required to open an existing encrypted image. |

### Exposed MCP Tools

The server exposes **8 tools** over stdio ([`src/bin/oifs_mcp.rs`](../../src/bin/oifs_mcp.rs)):

| Tool | Description | Parameters |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `write_file` | Write (create or overwrite) a file inside the OIFS sandbox image. Parent directories must already exist. | `path: string`, `content: string` |
| `read_file` | Read the contents of a file inside the OIFS sandbox image. Returns UTF-8 text content. | `path: string` |
| `list_dir` | List files and directories at a given path. Returns JSONL (one JSON object per line). | `path: string` |
| `mkdir` | Create a directory inside the OIFS sandbox image. Parent directories must exist. | `path: string` |
| `delete_file` | Delete a file from the OIFS sandbox image. | `path: string` |
| `truncate_file` | Truncate or extend a file to the specified size in bytes. | `path: string`, `size: number` |
| `append_file` | Append a line to a file (creates if not exists). Ideal for JSONL memory logs. Auto-adds newline if missing. | `path: string`, `content: string` |
| `status` | Show filesystem status: image path, total/used/free blocks, and fragmentation ratio. | (none) |

### MCP Tool Response Format

All tools return JSON strings. Successful responses include `"ok": true` plus tool-specific fields. Errors return `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}`. Responses are built with `serde_json` to ensure proper escaping.

#### Examples

**write_file success**:
```json
{"ok": true, "inode": 123, "bytes": 42}
```

**read_file success**: Returns raw UTF-8 string content (not JSON-wrapped).

**list_dir success** (JSONL):
```json
{"name": "notes", "kind": "dir", "size": 0}
{"name": "todo.txt", "kind": "file", "size": 128}
```

**status success**:
```json
{"image": "agent_memory.img", "total_blocks": 2560, "used_blocks": 100, "free_blocks": 2460, "fragmentation": 0.02}
```

**Error (any tool)**:
```json
{"ok": false, "error": "File not found: notes/missing.txt"}
```

---

## Network Mode and Master-Proxy Coordination

By default, OIFS runs in **Standalone** mode (no IPC). With `--ipc`, it runs in **Local** mode, creating a Unix domain socket under `/tmp/oifs_<name>_<hash>.sock`.

When operating over networked shared storage (NFS, Lustre, AWS EFS, or multi-node clusters):
- Adding `-n` / `--network` or specifying `--bind` switches to `SessionMode::Network`.
- The master binds to the specified address (default `127.0.0.1:0` for random ephemeral port).
- Proxies connect to the master via TCP.
- **Security**: The IPC transport is plain TCP without TLS. Binding to non-loopback addresses requires `--allow-remote-ipc` and should only be done inside a secure tunnel (WireGuard, IPsec, SSH).

---

## Related Pages

- [Configuration](../concepts/configuration.md) — Configuration file and environment variables
- [Quickstart](../quickstart.md) — Getting started with OIFS
- [Basic Operations](../workflows/basic_operations.md) — Common workflow examples
- [FSCK Workflow](../workflows/fsck_workflow.md) — Filesystem consistency checking

nodes.body:
# Testing and Formal Verification

OIFS employs a multi-tiered verification strategy designed to ensure absolute data durability, thread safety, and algorithmic correctness across the entire input space:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        Quality Assurance Strategy                        │
└────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
                                     │
        ┌────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┐
        ▼                            ▼                            ▼
┌──────────────────┐       ┌──────────────────┐       ┌──────────────────┐
│  Empirical Tests │       │  Shuttle Testing │       │   Formal Proofs  │
│  (Unit / Integ)  │       │ (Randomized DPOR)│       │   (Kani / TLA+)  │
├──────────────────┤       ├──────────────────┤       ├──────────────────┤
│ Concrete values  │       │ Permutes thread  │       │ Mathematical     │
│ End-to-end I/O   │       │ interleavings    │       │ proofs for ALL   │
│ FFI, CLI, MCP    │       │ Catches races &  │       │ symbolic inputs  │
│ 40+ test files   │       │ deadlocks        │       │ 131+ Kani proofs │
└──────────────────┘       └──────────────────┘       └──────────────────┘
        ▲                            ▲                            ▲
        │                            │                            │
        └────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┘
                                     ▼
                        ┌──────────────────────────┐
                        │  Property / Fuzz Tests   │
                        │        (Bolero)          │
                        ├──────────────────────────┤
                        │ Arbitrary input gen      │
                        │ Roundtrip invariants     │
                        │ 16+ harnesses            │
                        └──────────────────────────┘
```

1. **Empirical Test Suites (`tests/`)**: 40+ test files validate end-to-end integration, CLI operations, FFI memory safety, pluggable I/O engines, cross-platform endianness, encryption, defragmentation, fsck, MCP server integration, crash safety, network mode, FUSE, and format migration.
2. **Controlled Concurrency Exploration (Shuttle)**: Uses DPOR (Dynamic Partial Order Reduction) to systematically explore thread interleavings, exposing heisenbugs, race conditions, and deadlocks.
3. **Property-Based Fuzzing (Bolero)**: Generates arbitrary inputs to verify roundtrip invariants, panic-freedom, and semantic equivalence across parsers, codecs, and state machines.
4. **Formal Verification (AWS Kani Rust Verifier & TLA+)**: Utilizes SAT/SMT solvers (CBMC/CaDiCaL) and formal specification to mathematically prove safety invariants across all possible symbolic inputs and concurrent protocol transitions.
5. **Benchmarks**: Ad-hoc performance tests for directory scaling, journal overhead, flush latency, and implementation comparisons.

---

## Test Suite Structure

The `tests/` directory organizes ~40 test cases across specialized functional domains:

| Test File | Verification Scope | Key Invariants Checked |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `tests/integration_test.rs` | Core File & Dir Operations | Inode creation, direct/indirect writes, truncation, reads |
| `tests/read_at_test.rs` | Zero-Copy Random Slices | Direct mmap slice copies, EOF bounds, encrypted/compressed reads |
| `tests/seekable_chunked_concurrency_test.rs` | Seekable 64K Multithreading | 16-thread sliced reads, parallel partitioned chunk writes, COW extent swaps |
| `tests/concurrent_same_file_test.rs` | POSIX OpenMode Concurrency | 16-thread simultaneous `create_file` (exactly 1 wins, 15 get `EEXIST`) |
| `tests/io_engine_test.rs` | Pluggable I/O Engine (P3.2) | Backend selection (Mmap, Pread, io_uring), batched reads, extent coalescing |
| `tests/rwlock_concurrency_test.rs` | Concurrent Read Scaling | 16 parallel reader threads without lock contention |
| `tests/endianness_and_portability_test.rs` | Endian Invariance | Involution $T(T(x)) = x$, Big/Little-Endian integer parity |
| `tests/filter_test.rs` | Pre-Compression Filters | Roundtrip fidelity for Delta, ByteShuffle, BitShuffle |
| `tests/encryption_test.rs` | Cryptography Subsystem | XChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD integrity, SIV filename encryption |
| `tests/fsck_test.rs` | Consistency Scanner | Detection of orphan inodes, leaked blocks, and cross-links |
| `tests/fsck_extended_test.rs` | Extended FSCK | Orphan, leaked, missing, cross-linked block detection |
| `tests/defrag_test.rs` | Online Defragmentation | 3-step atomic rename, metadata preservation, rollback safety |
| `tests/defrag_seekable_chunk_test.rs` | Seekable Defrag | COW extent swap crash safety |
| `tests/cli_test.rs` | Command-Line Interface | Argument parsing, password prompts, `--json` format |
| `tests/cli_all_commands_test.rs` | Full CLI Coverage | All subcommands, edge cases |
| `tests/cli_concurrent_process_test.rs` | Multi-Process CLI | IPC mode, master election, concurrent puts/gets |
| `tests/cli_extended_test.rs` | Extended CLI | Additional flags, error paths |
| `tests/cli_mkdir_test.rs` | mkdir CLI | Directory creation via CLI |
| `tests/cli_recursive_test.rs` | Recursive Operations | Recursive delete, copy |
| `tests/cli_rm_test.rs` | rm CLI | File/directory removal |
| `tests/ffi_test.rs` | C Shared Library ABI | Handle lifecycle, callback directory streaming, backend switching |
| `tests/ffi_c_cpp_test.rs` | C/C++ Compiler Integration | Strict `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror`, C11 & C++17/20 |
| `tests/ffi_delete_test.rs` | FFI Delete | Delete file via FFI |
| `tests/ffi_extended_test.rs` | Extended FFI | Additional FFI APIs |
| `tests/ffi_robustness_test.rs` | FFI Robustness | Null pointers, oversized buffers, use-after-close |
| `tests/ffi_version_test.rs` | FFI Version | Version handshake, library path reporting |
| `tests/cpp_api_test.rs` | C++ API | RAII wrappers, lambda callbacks, `std::span` integration |
| `tests/async_and_ffi_test.rs` | Async FFI | Thread-local error state, concurrent operations |
| `tests/mcp_server_test.rs` | MCP Server | Protocol compliance, tool invocation |
| `tests/crash_safety_test.rs` | Crash Safety | Flush persistence, drop flush, block overflow safety |
| `tests/durability_test.rs` | Durability Modes | Lazy vs Strict durability guarantees |

| `tests/shuttle_concurrency_test.rs` | DPOR Concurrency | Randomized thread interleaving, race/deadlock detection |
| `tests/fuse_test.rs` | FUSE Protocol | In-memory FUSE operations, handle table, readdir pagination |

| `tests/backward_compatibility_test.rs` | Format Migration | v1/v2 image read, upgrade to v3 |
| `tests/format_migration_test.rs` | Format Migration | Inode v1→v3, superblock layout evolution |
| `tests/session_and_cache_test.rs` | Session/Cache | Master/proxy, cache coherence, storage mode matrix |
| `tests/session_edge_cases_test.rs` | Session Edge Cases | Failover, reconnection, password handling |
| `tests/session_ipc_test.rs` | Session IPC | Unix domain socket, master election |
